title: 'Nothing impossible' as NI begin long road to Brazil
description: Northern Ireland defenders Nat Johnson and Rebecca Holloway tell BBC Sport NI of their dream of reaching a first ever Women's World Cup as NI go through the play-offs.
fullText:
A World Cup staged in Brazil is the stuff of dreams for any footballer and the chance to experience that is on offer for Northern Ireland as they begin their play-off journey against Portugal with hope of securing a spot at next year's tournament.

It will be a difficult ask for Michael McArdle's side, which has been hit by a spate of injuries and features five new faces, but there is a quiet confidence in the group before what will be, for some of them, the biggest games in their careers to date.

First up, in what is set to be an arduous journey in search of a World Cup debut, is Friday's home leg at Inver Park (19:30 BST) against the Portuguese.

"When you're growing up, Brazil is the place to be, it's the home of football. It really doesn't get much better than that," said Norwich City defender Natalie Johnson.

"The fact that we are at this point and that it could be a reality, you don't need much more motivation than that.

"There's a lot on the line, but we are taking it one game at a time and I think if you look at it that way, nothing is impossible. Obviously there is that dream at the end of it, but we're focused on the game in front of us."

Family, football and Dalglish - what drives NI boss McArdle?

What will new call-ups bring to Northern Ireland?

Elmore and Grant named in Northern Ireland squad

As one of the lowest-ranked European sides in the play-offs, it is a difficult route to next summer's tournament for Northern Ireland.

If they overcome Portugal they will then face Croatia or Iceland in the next round. If they make it through those games, they will likely have an inter-continental play-off to make it the whole way to Brazil.

Portugal inflicted two defeats on in NI in Euro 2025 qualifying and sit 28 places higher in the Fifa world rankings, but Johnson and her side are not daunted by the task in front of them and instead want to embrace it.

"We absolutely believe these games are winnable," she added.

"We have a lot of experience in this team and the young players coming in bring their own individual experience and they really add to the squad. It's a good balance and we are going in to get something out of this.

"Any Portugal side is going to be very technical and we're expecting a very fast-paced game. We're going to have to be at our best to face that, quick football, and that's what we're working towards.

"On paper it might look like there is a big gap between the teams, but at the end of the day, it is a game of football and I think particularly on our home pitch it will be a much more level playing field."

Birmingham City defender Rebecca Holloway is one of the few survivors from the squad that qualified for Euro 2022, NI's first major tournament.

There have been a lot of changes to the squad since, but Holloway is excited for the future rather than dwelling on past achievements.

"It feels like a long time ago in a way, especially when you look at how much the squad has changed, but I think that's also what is very exciting," she said.

"It's like a new generation coming through and I think it's also important that we have some experienced players here to help those new faces. We're excited to see what they can do and encourage them to play with confidence and freedom and do what they are good at.

"We're slowly closing the gap on Portugal and the so-called bigger nations. They had a narrow 2-1 win over us at home in 2024 after a 4-0 away defeat, I think that shows that we are getting closer."

McArdle's youthful side do not have far to look for inspiration as to how to punch above their weight.

After assembling in camp on Monday, the team watched Northern Ireland's men's side 0-0 draw with Georgia.

That stalemate ensured Michael O'Neill's side stayed top of their Nations League group after picking up eight points from four games without conceding a goal.

"It was brilliant watching them play with such youth and energy and the exciting football that they are playing.

"This younger generation play with no fear and I think that is what the men's senior team are doing.

"I am hoping the young players see that and we can adopt the same attitude. I think we were all watching thinking we can't wait to do this on Friday."

title: How can home nations reach Women's World Cup?
description: England, Wales, Northern Ireland, Scotland and the Republic of Ireland are among those hoping to qualify for next year's Women's World Cup. What awaits them in the play-offs?
fullText:
England must get through two rounds of home and away ties to qualify for the Women's World Cup in Brazil.

Sarina Wiegman's European champions will play Greece in Crete in round one of the play-offs, with the first leg on Friday, 9 October at 17:30 BST.

The second leg will be played at home, at King Power Stadium in Leicester, on Tuesday, 13 October at 19:30 BST.

Commentary for both England matches will be on BBC Radio 5 Live.

Should England beat Greece over two games, they will face the winners of Slovakia v Ukraine, with the away fixture played first.

The exact dates of the potential second-leg fixtures are to be confirmed, although they will take place between 26 November and 5 December 2026.

England head coach Wiegman named her initial squad last month, with Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly notable absentees.

When asked why they were left out, Wiegman said: "They have not been playing to their full potential.

"Of course, I still believe in these players. They are really good and have shown so much for us."

Wiegman told BBC Radio 5 Live: "That is also why I didn't pick them this time, because they have not played to their potential in my opinion in the last couple of weeks.

"I had those conversations with them and that was very hard to take. They took it well and, of course, they want to work on that."

All you need to know about 2027 Women's World Cup

Northern Ireland, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland are also involved in the play-offs as they chase World Cup places.

As with England, they are in action on Friday.

In round one, Wales face Albania at 17:00 BST - with coverage on BBC Two Wales from 16:45 BST.

Scotland play the Czech Republic at 18:00 BST, available to watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC Alba.

Northern Ireland take on Portugal at 19:00 BST, available on BBC iPlayer.

The Republic of Ireland will play Kazakhstan at 12:00 BST.

Despite England securing five wins from their six qualifying matches, world champions Spain finished top of the Lionesses' group and secured the one automatic spot.

Wiegman said: "We knew what the play-offs would look like and, while we're pleased with the draw against Greece, the focus now is on making sure we're really well prepared.

"We want to dominate games and have a lot of the ball and that's something we will prepare for carefully."

England did not want to go through the play-offs but were given an unkind draw in the qualifying groups when they met world champions Spain.

However, Wiegman's side are in a strong position for the play-offs and will fancy their chances against Greece, who sit 55 places beneath them in the Fifa world rankings.

England also beat potential round two opponents Ukraine in both matches in the qualifying group stage, with an aggregate 9-1 score.

Northern Ireland face a tricky tie against a talented young squad from Portugal in round one. Portugal twice beat Northern Ireland in Euro 2025 qualifying.

Their task gets even harder if they make it through to round two, with potential opponents Iceland proving to be difficult to break down in their matches against England this year.

Scotland are hoping to reach just their second Women's World Cup finals, after a 2019 appearance. They failed to qualify in 2023 but have performed well this year, including drawing with Belgium, showing that they can compete with Europe's strongest teams.

They would need to produce their best in round two if they meet big-hitters Sweden, who have been semi-finalists in the past two Women's World Cups.

Wales have never beaten a top-20 ranked nation in a competitive fixture and are likely to need to do so to qualify.

There is optimism, though, as Rhian Wilkinson's side thrashed play-off opponents Albania 4-0 in their qualifying group.

Elsewhere, having performed superbly in qualifying, the Republic of Ireland have a tough play-off route with Belgium potentially waiting in round two.

First, Carla Ward's side will have to navigate a 3,100-mile trip to Kazakhstan, to tackle relatively unknown opposition.

title: She made India fall in love with women's cricket - now her era as captain is over
description: The skipper who led India to the historic 2025 World Cup win has stepped down from her role in all three formats.
fullText:
When Harmanpreet Kaur scored that unforgettable World Cup century against Australia in the 2017 semi-final, she not only changed the course of a match but the trajectory of women's cricket in India.

India went on to lose the final to England that year but women's cricket no longer remained a passing pursuit for the average Indian fan.

That dogged zeal to win she infused into the team helped them lift India's first women's World Cup trophy - the same feat that had eluded them in 2017 - in emphatic fashion eight years later.

Less than a year on, and within weeks of victories in the Asia Cup and the Asian Games, she has relinquished the captaincy, ending an era in which she became the team's most influential leader and one of the most recognisable figures in the sport.

Star opener Smriti Mandhana, her long-time deputy, has been appointed captain across all formats.

Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) secretary Devajit Saikia, coach Amol Muzumdar, Harmanpreet and Mandhana attended the review meeting at which the leadership change was ratified. The transition, however, was not entirely seamless.

Reports suggest the 37-year-old Harmanpreet was willing to relinquish the T20 captaincy immediately, but was keen to continue leading the side in One-Day Internationals and Tests so that younger players could benefit from her experience.

The BCCI, however, was intent on a younger person at the helm and opted for the 30-year-old Mandhana.

In some ways, the move mirrors the BCCI's decision to replace Suryakumar Yadav as captain of the men's T20 side shortly after India won the World Cup earlier this year, with the captaincy passing to Shreyas Iyer.

Harmanpreet's future as captain had become a subject of intense debate in cricketing circles after India's below-par performance at the T20 World Cup in England a few months ago.

Her own poor form with the bat amplified concerns and prompted the BCCI to consider changes that could help the team meet the growing challenges of a women's game that continues to expand rapidly around the world.

Approaching her 38th birthday, and after almost a decade at the helm, Harmanpreet found herself under increasing scrutiny as her form dipped.

Opinion on whether she should continue as captain was sharply divided among former women players and captains.

Former cricketer Diana Edulji, among the most respected names in the game, felt Harmanpreet had done everything that could reasonably have been expected of her and that it was time for a younger captain to take over. Former captain Anjum Chopra, meanwhile, argued that Harmanpreet's experience remained invaluable and that she should stay on.

Sensing that the BCCI was strongly inclined towards a change, Harmanpreet opted to step down during the review meeting. She later announced her decision in an emotional Instagram post.

"I feel I have done my duty. I gave this team everything I had," she wrote.

"Now, it is time for me to turn the page… Blood. Sweat. Sacrifice. Pride. I gave it all. Now, I'm ready to play for the love of the game again.

"Captaincy ends, the journey continues."

Harmanpreet's intention to continue playing now leaves the BCCI with another decision to make about her future.

In Suryakumar Yadav's case, he not only lost the captaincy but also his place in India's T20 side. Given the depth of talent available in the men's game, it was easier for Ajit Agarkar and his fellow selectors to take what was always likely to be a contentious decision.

The situation in the women's game is different. Despite Harmanpreet's modest recent form, replacing a player of her experience and stature may not be straightforward, as the talent pipeline is not yet as deep as it is in men's cricket.

Whatever the future holds, Harmanpreet has scripted among the more memorable careers in women's cricket. Spanning more than two decades, it is a journey marked by significant achievements and milestones.

Born into a family of modest means in Punjab's Moga city, Harmanpreet developed a passion for cricket at an early age.

Her family's support was vital in the early years, but her rise to national recognition came after she joined the Railways - a transition facilitated by Diana Edulji - and moved to Mumbai.

The superior facilities and greater professionalism associated with Mumbai's sporting culture helped accelerate her development.

She made her India debut in 2009 at the age of 20 and has remained an integral part of the national side across formats ever since.

An all-rounder for the better part of her first decade in cricket, she made herself indispensable to the side with her explosive middle-order batting, crafty off-spin and sharp fielding skills.

Her blistering century against Australia in the semi-final of the 2017 Women's ODI World Cup remains one of the defining knocks in the history of the women's game. India went on to lose to England in the final, but beating Australia was a monumental hurdle overcome.

That century also helped spark wider interest in women's cricket in India, and transformed Harmanpreet into a household name.

The second decade of her career showcased her prowess both as batter and captain. Having succeeded Mithali Raj as T20 captain in 2016, Harmanpreet assumed charge across all formats in 2022 and went on to guide India to some of the greatest successes in its history.

Her leadership was marked by an aggressive pursuit of victory. That fearless approach instilled confidence and ambition in her teammates, helping the team overcome even the previously unbeatable Australians, most memorably in the semi-final of the 2025 ODI World Cup.

Unlike in 2017, Harmanpreet couldn't get a hundred on that occasion, but her innings of 89 was a stellar effort as captain. Combined with Jemimah Rodrigues's century, it helped India secure a famous victory over their arch rivals.

India then defeated South Africa in the final to reach what many regard as the pinnacle of achievement in the history of Indian women's cricket.

With multiple titles and trophies won under her leadership, Harmanpreet leaves behind a formidable legacy for her successor, Smriti Mandhana, to emulate.

title: Toone comes into England squad as Bronze withdraws
description: Manchester United midfielder Ella Toone receives a late England call-up for this month's World Cup play-off games against Greece.
fullText:
Ella Toone has received a late call into the England squad for this month's Women's World Cup play-off ties against Greece.

Manchester United midfielder Toone, and Arsenal winger Chloe Kelly, were omitted from the initial squad with manager Sarina Wiegman saying "they have not played to their potential in my opinion in the last couple of weeks".

Toone has scored 24 goals in 69 senior England appearances, winning Euro 2022 and Euro 2025 as well as starting in England's 2023 World Cup final defeat by Spain.

Toone said after being left out of the squad: "It's been a really difficult week. It's not the news that any footballer wants."

Meanwhile, Chelsea defender Lucy Bronze has left the squad and will return to her club to manage a minor injury sustained in league action last weekend against West Ham.

The Lionesses arrived in Crete on Wednesday evening to prepare for Friday's first leg against Greece at the Pankritio Stadium in Heraklion.

The second leg takes place at Leicester City's King Power Stadium on Tuesday, 13 October.

The winners face either Slovakia or Ukraine on 26 November and 5 December in a two-legged play-off to decide which team progresses to next year's Women's World Cup, which is being held in Brazil from 24 June to 25 July.

title: England to host 2031 Netball World Cup
description: England will host the Netball World Cup for the fourth time in 2031, when the sport's pinnacle event is held at Manchester's Co-op Live arena.
fullText:
England will host the Netball World Cup for the fourth time in 2031.

The quadrennial tournament will be held at Manchester's Co-op Live indoor arena, World Netball and England Netball announced on Thursday.

Liverpool staged the event when England last hosted in 2019.

World Netball president Liz Nicholl said: "After reviewing their strong bid, I am confident England Netball will host another thrilling international event, and I am excited to see what we can achieve together in 2031 and beyond."

Eastbourne put on the inaugural tournament in 1963, with Birmingham staging the 1995 edition.

England reached a World Cup final for the first time in 2023, but the Roses were denied a first title by 12-time winners Australia in Cape Town.

England also finished as runners-up in 1975, when the tournament was contested in a league format.

Baroness Sue Campbell, chair of England Netball, said: "To have the best netball players in the world coming to Manchester is a hugely exciting prospect, and I know the city will give them the welcome they deserve.

"This is a fantastic opportunity not only to showcase our sport on the biggest stage, but also to inspire the next generation of players and fans."

England Netball chief executive Fran Connolly said the tournament would provide "a powerful platform to grow the visibility, profile and impact of women's sport and netball across the UK".

The announcement comes in England Netball's centenary year.

The Co-op Live arena hosted this year's Netball Super League Grand Final between AO Thunder and London Pulse, which was played in front of more than 8,000 fans.

title: Family, football and Dalglish - what drives NI boss McArdle?
description: BBC Sport NI's Andy Gray sits down with Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle to discuss his long career before his biggest managerial test in the World Cup play-offs.
fullText:
As Michael McArdle sits down for an interview with BBC Sport at Windsor Park, he cuts a relaxed figure.

The Scot had just announced his squad for the World Cup play-off with Portugal, for what will be the biggest game of his managerial career to date.

McArdle has only been in the Northern Ireland hot seat since March, when he was announced as Tanya Oxtoby's permanent successor, but has more than 25 years of experience working in football.

There's a clear passion for what he is doing, as he balances the reality of playing one of Europe's top-ranked sides with the dreams of reaching a first World Cup just months into his new role.

But there is one word that keeps cropping up across various topics - family.

McArdle, 48, was born and bred in Moodiesburn to the east of Glasgow, and still lives there to this day.

He met his wife, Tammy, in the village when they were both on the same paper round at the age of 12, and they have now been married for 28 years.

He has three children, Connor, Mya and Cole, and is about to become a grandad for the first time. It's clear how much his family means to him.

But when he talks about family, it's not just in terms of his own life. It is an embodiment of what he is trying to achieve with Northern Ireland.

"Family's crucial to me. We're all a family when we represent the country," he said.

"That's a family of players and a family of staff, but also as an ecosystem and domestic game.

"We're all the one family when we're together and that's a message that will always be strong while I'm at the helm."

What will new call-ups bring to Northern Ireland?

Elmore and Grant named in Northern Ireland squad

If Northern Ireland are to make it to their first World Cup in Brazil then there are a number of hurdles they will need to clear.

It would perhaps surpass even the fairytale of qualifying for Euro 2022, when Kenny Shiels led a squad largely made up of amateur players to the promised land.

A change in format has made replicating that feat more difficult, and if Northern Ireland can beat Portugal over two legs then they will face Croatia or, more likely, Iceland.

The Portuguese and Iceland have beaten Northern Ireland over the past two years or so - both quite convincingly.

Even if McArdle's young squad can defy the odds, they will likely face an additional inter-continental play-off in February due to their rankings. It's a tall order.

But that does not stop McArdle and Northern Ireland from dreaming. If anything, it is to be encouraged.

"I think the dream piece is crucial, so we've dreamed about how we get there and what it'll feel like when we do it.

"The other piece of it is the reality. We know it's a highly challenging task first of all to get through Portugal."

McArdle talks about moments within matches, and working with his staff to plan for in-game scenarios.

There's also the excitement that comes with such a big match, and McArdle admits he is "loving" his time in charge.

"You look forward to every game but it's one of those ties that gives you the opportunity to test yourself at the highest level.

"Also the excitement of possibly achieving something and punching above our weight, which we're special at doing."

In his career in football, McArdle has held a number of coaching, academy and development positions.

Before he joined Northern Ireland, he was head of elite women's football at the Scottish FA, and also had a brief interim spell in charge of their senior team.

While the belief is there, McArdle knows he is working on something longer-term, and that can be seen in the make-up of a young squad, which has been hit by a number of injuries to senior players.

While his first two international windows came in quick succession, with two victories over Malta followed by losses to Turkey and Switzerland, the summer has allowed him to spend time around the Women's Premiership in Northern Ireland, building relationships with players and those working in the league.

"I was still getting to know them as people, not as footballers, so that was really important for me to build those relationships.

"Not just the players, either. Getting to know the head coaches a bit more and some of the clubs at boardroom level, to understand how can I serve them and help the club evolution, the domestic league and pathways as well."

While captain Simone Magill is a big loss for the play-offs, she will be with the group for the camp as she builds towards a return to action and provide experience to what is a young group of players.

Not only that, but she will have her newborn daughter, Skye, with her for the duration. McArdle says having those moments are "special".

"Having Simone, Mark and Skye on camp is great. First of all for Simone and Mark to experience what the future is like when Simone's representing Northern Ireland.

"It gives us that window of opportunity and it's something we've planned together over the summer months.

"I think that's crucial because it's one thing knowing the players and the girls that represent us, but also the families that support them as well.

"I'm very passionate about that and I don't underestimate the power of it."

Given the themes throughout, it's no surprise what drives McArdle.

He grew up idolising the likes of Kenny Dalglish, who once was a loan player from Celtic at Cumbernauld United juniors near where he grew up.

His coaching influences are close to home too, and he cites Michael O'Halloran, a youth coach in Glasgow, and Sir Alex Ferguson, who was a "god" coming from the east end of the city.

Further afield, the likes of Arrigo Sacchi - whose AC Milan side he used to watch on VHS in the 90s - Jose Mourinho and Rafa Benitez have all factored into his thinking.

"What drew me towards Sacchi, Mourinho and Benitez was not just the tactical side of the game, but how they managed it and their leadership.

"They didn't play professionally and it kind of aligned with myself, although I didn't realise at the time."

But it's in Moodiesburn where his DNA is, and it is the values he learned there that have shaped him into the coach he is today.

"Growing up in the village and growing up as a family I was always going to care for people and be in a service role.

"It was always going to be my calling. I'm just blessed that football has given me the opportunity to develop a knowledge and skill set to work at the highest level of an industry."

McArdle's passion for football is clear, but family also plays a role in helping him escape the demands of the job.

He goes to the theatre with his daughter, Mya, or to the cinema or concerts with Tammy.

A sports fan, he also goes and watches his sons play football, without the stresses of management and coaching.

"Representing my family is everything to me.

"We've stayed in the same village all our lives. You represent the village as well and that becomes a big piece of what we do.

"So those aspects of family fuel you."

title: Republic of Ireland boss Ward focused on World Cup amid Villa link
description: Republic of Ireland manager Carla Ward says that "nothing is tempting" her away from her job as they prepare for a World Cup qualifying double-header against Kazakhstan.
fullText:
Republic of Ireland manager Carla Ward says that her focus is on reaching the Women's World Cup amid speculation linking her to a move back to the Women's Super League.

The Republic have a chance to book a spot at next summer's finals in Brazil when they face a play-off against Kazakhstan before, if they progress, a two-legged final against either Belgium or Poland.

Ward, who replaced Eileen Gleeson in January 2025, has been linked with the vacant post at her former club Aston Villa. However, she insists leading the Republic of Ireland to the World Cup is her primary ambition.

"Nothing is tempting when I'm in this job, you know I love this job and I love working here," Ward said.

"I don't think anything can take my attention away from these next four games so it's not a conversation and it's not anything I would entertain.

"My heart and my focus, I came here to try and get to a World Cup and that's all I'm going to think about for the next four games."

The Republic of Ireland made history when they qualified for the World Cup in 2023 for the first time ever. However, they were unable to progress from the group, beaten by co-hosts Australia and Canada, before drawing with Nigeria.

Three years on, Ward now has the chance to lead the team back to the biggest stage in international football.

"You've seen how I've spoken in the last two years and with immense pride in this job," she continued.

"I'm here because I want to get to a World Cup and I think we've made tremendous strides and steps as a nation, and it would be the cherry on the cake, but, look we've got four games, four cup finals.

"We have to give everything, blood, sweat and tears. We have to leave everything out there in everything we do and if we do that, we've got every chance."

The two-legged tie against Kazakhstan begins with a trip to the Astana Arena on Friday, 9 October (12:00 BST) before the return fixture in Cork four days later.

The Republic of Ireland are unbeaten at Pairc Ui Chaoimh, but Ward is taking nothing for granted against a Kazakhstan side ranked 98th in the world.

"We have to go up another level, we have to make sure that we're performing, and we're focused at the highest level.

"If we do that then we'll get the job done. We've got an unbelievable squad that are hugely talented and they will look after each other.

"I think anyone that comes in that will know their role I think we're really clear with what we do, what we want and how we play."

Ward will have to make changes, with captain Katie McCabe and Marissa Sheva both suspended for the first leg, while the experienced Denise O'Sullivan is also unavailable.

Tara O'Hanlon is out with a hamstring injury and Saoirse Noonan has also been ruled out of both games with an ankle problem.

Meanwhile, Crystal Palace midfielder Shanade Hopcroft has been called into the squad for the first time.

Despite the absence of multiple key leaders, Ward says this is a chance for others to shine.

"No matter who plays, naturally when you take the likes of Katie and Denise out of your team, they're two big leaders but that's an opportunity for players to step up.

"Katie's here for a reason, she's got a big part to play off the pitch, and she will and she'll lead the group as she normally does.

"Then it'll be over to those that go out there and I have full belief in every single one of this group to go and get the job done."

title: 'Bring the magic' - Scotland's Ross eyes World Cup dream
description: Scotland assistant coach Leanne Ross never played at a World Cup but thinks the current squad has what it takes to get through the play-offs for Brazil 2027.
fullText:
Leanne Ross is Scotland's most decorated player, earning 133 international caps across a career which garnered 14 league titles and 13 major cup medals, but still the national team's assistant coach wants more.

Having reached the 2017 European Championship, Ross was part of the first women's squad to compete at a major tournament, but one thing has eluded her. A World Cup.

Ross retired after the Euros, meaning she did not take part in the 2019 edition in France, but her dream has not been dashed.

Scotland are a wee bit away from booking flights and hotels for Brazil 2027. Up next is a round one play-off double-header against Czech Republic, live on the BBC, but the excitement is building.

"It would be huge," Ross said the day before the Scots travel to Pardubice, east of Prague, for the first leg. "I never got to do it as a player, reaching that World Cup stage.

"I played in the Euro finals and that was an amazing experience and just topped off my career as a player, but to go and do it as part of the coaching staff, it would be such a proud moment."

Scots recall 'versatile' Kerr & Thomas for World Cup play-offs

Ross is part of the SWNT furniture, having seamlessly shifted into a coaching role following her stellar playing career, so she knows a thing or two about what makes the team tick.

She also knows what its like to taste play-off pain.

Two years ago, it was Finland who denied Scotland a place at the 2025 Euros. Before that, Republic of Ireland romped to the World Cup in Australia.

Many in the squad still carry the scars of both final-hurdle failures.

From the outside, it's fair to fear a repeat, with heavyweights Sweden potentially lying in wait in round two.

But Ross isn't thinking like that. Instead, her confidence of "getting back to where we want to be" stems from the squad bringing their "magic".

"The progress that we're making and the way that we're playing at this moment is a real good opportunity for us to do that," Ross - who is Glasgow City head coach - said of ending the team's eight-year wait for a return to a major tournament.

"You look at the quality we have, the teams that they're playing for, the environments that they're in and individually them bringing their magic into this team and putting that all together.

"I think it's a really exciting time for Scotland with the players we have. We need to make sure we give them the platform to go, play and get themselves on that world stage."

title: Davies' 'extra motivation' after Euros heartbreak
description: Defender Mayzee Davies says missing Wales' first major tournament at Euro 2025 with a serious knee injury has given her extra motivation for the World Cup play-offs.
fullText:
Wales defender Mayzee Davies says missing Euro 2025 through injury has given her extra motivation for the World Cup play-offs.

The 20-year-old suffered an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) knee injury on international duty in May 2025 which kept her out of action for 13 months.

She missed Wales' historic first ever major tournament appearance and now is determined to reach the 2027 World Cup.

Wales face Albania in Shkoder on Friday, 9 October in the first leg of their semi-final with the return fixture in Llanelli four days later.

"It was just so sad for everyone, even in my street, it affected us.

"I'd just broken through [into the team] and I was 18 going to my first major tournament.

"It was horrible, and I think everyone close to me felt it.

"And at the time, I didn't realise how bad it was until I looked back and went how did I get through that?

The Manchester City defender returned to action with Wales for their final two group qualifiers in June against Montenegro and Czech Republic.

And now she is determined not to miss out again.

"I want to get to the World Cup because obviously I missed out last time, so I want to feel what it's like to go to a major tournament with Wales.

"It does give me that extra motivation. I love playing for Wales and I think we're quite a passionate country anyway.

"So I think to play in a World Cup for Wales, obviously in Brazil, it would be amazing.

"Not just for me and my family, obviously coming off the back of the injury as well, I think it would make it extra special if we got there."

Davies admits she found her 13-month recovery tough and worried she may never return.

"I think once I had the surgery I was literally stuck on the sofa, I couldn't do anything on my own.

"I was like, how am I ever going to like be a footballer again at this stage?

"But I had good people around me, team-mates, my family, and then it does get better.

"One day you just wake up and you're like, 'oh, I can start to walk again now'."

Wales have suffered a host of injury withdrawals ahead of the Albania ties, losing a number of key players including Ceri Holland ands Hayley Ladd.

But facing a team 37 places below them in the Fifa world rankings, Davies knows there can be no excuses for Wales as they bid to set up a play-off final against either Romania or Norway.

"Obviously this camp we've had a lot of injuries to like more experienced players, the usual faces," she said.

"But I think everyone in this group now, you have to make sure all the new people feel a part of the team and feel valued.

"She [Head Coach Rhian Wilkinson] said at the end of the day, we always respect every opponent we come up against.

"But this is a must-win game and we can't dwell on who's not here.

"We have to work with who's here now and obviously everyone has their role and we've just got to get the job done."

title: England forward Packer to miss North America tour
description: Two-time World Cup winner Marlie Packer will not travel with England to North America this month for Tests against Canada and the United States.
fullText:
Two-time World Cup winner Marlie Packer will not travel with England to North America this month for Tests against Canada and the United States.

The Harlequins back-rower will remain in the United Kingdom with her partner and Red Roses team-mate Rosie Galligan due to give birth.

England face Canada on 17 and 24 October (both 00:00 BST starts) before playing the USA in one-off match on 30 October (21:15 BST).

England are boosted by the return of Kelsey Clifford for the North American tour, with the Saracens prop returning from a hamstring injury.

The Red Roses continue a tough run of fixtures after playing three matches in September, beating Australia and New Zealand but ending their record-breaking winning streak with a draw against Canada.

England head coach John Mitchell described their home Tests with Canada and the Black Ferns as "humdingers that could have gone either way."

The Tests against Canada in Toronto and Ottawa are being viewed by England as the culmination of a self-titled three-Test series.

Mitchell described his expectations for the squad: "The 32 players travelling to North America have a great opportunity to elevate our connections as a squad because playing away from home requires togetherness.

"We have shown a real hunger to compete and improve, and we're excited to rip into our preparations and continue our rivalry with Canada in Toronto."

England also confirmed that Delaney Burns, Haidee Head and Sophie McQueen would not travel due to injury.

title: Connor out, Lewis in as England name World Cup squad
description: Leeds Rhinos half-back Jake Connor is left out of England's Rugby League World Cup squad, with Hull KR's Mikey Lewis beating him to a place.
fullText:
Jake Connor missed out on a Rugby League World Cup spot by a "small margin" as England seek the players who can best stick to their gameplan, head coach Brian McDermott says.

Leeds Rhinos half-back Connor, the 2025 Super League Man of Steel, was left out of the 23-man squad for the tournament - to be held largely in Australia - with Hull KR's Mikey Lewis making the cut instead.

For Connor, it is another England disappointment to follow his controversial omission from the squad for last autumn's home series against Australia.

"Jake Connor missed out on selection by a small margin and it came down to who I think can best stick to the game plan and attack plan," McDermott said.

The 31-year-old had been expected to make the squad after being talked up by McDermott and enjoying a strong domestic season.

But Hull KR's Lewis, who endured an inconsistent year, has done enough to convince McDermott that he should join captain George Williams, the Warrington stand-off, and Wigan's Harry Smith as half-back options.

England begin their World Cup campaign against Tonga in Perth on 17 October, before facing France in the same city on 24 October and then Papua New Guinea in Wollongong on 30 October.

England squad: Matty Ashton (Warrington Wolves), AJ Brimson (Gold Coast Titans), Ben Currie (Warrington Wolves), Zach Eckersley (Wigan Warriors), Herbie Farnworth (Dolphins), Ethan Havard (Wigan Warriors), Max King (Bulldogs), Morgan Knowles (Dolphins), Mikey Lewis (Hull KR), Jez Litten (Hull KR), Junior Nsemba (Wigan Warriors), Brad O'Neill (Wigan Warriors), Kai Pearce-Paul (Wests Tigers), Victor Radley (Sydney Roosters), Hugo Savala (Sydney Roosters), Harry Smith (Wigan Warriors), Morgan Smithies (Canberra Raiders), Luke Thompson (Wigan Warriors), Sam Walters (Wigan Warriors), Ben Talty (Brisbane Broncos), Jack Welsby (St Helens), George Williams (Warrington Wolves), Dom Young (Newcastle Knights)

Australia-born Strange in England World Cup squad

Hawkins among five World Cup winners in England squad

There has been much debate about which half-backs would make the England squad after McDermott said last month that he would probably take three to the World Cup, and that captain Williams - who is heading to Australia to join NRL club Dolphins after the tournament - would be one of them.

McDermott said: "Jake has had a really good year. He had an outstanding year last year and got Man of Steel.

"What I've got is a squad full of players who I believe will best play to the game style, the attack plan or game model we identified many weeks ago, that I think we need to compete with the leading nations.

"We can't do the usual things, and I made this a point when I took the job. We've got to play with a point of difference.

"I've got a squad here who I believe are best suited to the attack plan and game model I think England need to play."

Explaining his decision to select Lewis, McDermott added: "I've picked a group of player that have recent history of playing in finals, winning finals, delivering when it matters.

"Mikey Lewis won a World Club Challenge at the start of this year and guided his team to a Challenge Cup final.

"I get he wasn't in the best of shape towards the back of the year and incurred a couple of bans but again, I'll just point people to the attack plan and game model I think England need to have to compete with the leading nations."

When he replaced Shaun Wane as head coach, McDermott indicated that he was keen to use heritage players - those who qualify for England through family background - to ensure the strongest possible squad.

He has called up two uncapped Australia-born players - versatile back Hugo Savala, part of Sydney Roosters' NRL Grand Final-winning squad, and Brisbane Broncos' front-rower Ben Talty.

Bulldogs prop Max King, born in Huddersfield while his Australian father David was a player there, also earns a first call-up. Victor Radley and AJ Brimson complete the Australia-born contingent in the squad.

Grand Final winners Wakefield have no players in the squad, with Tom Johnstone, Mike McMeeken, Caleb Hamlin-Uele and Jake Trueman all needing time to recover from injuries.

"It's a real shame that the Wakefield boys aren't available," McDermott said. "There's nothing we or they can do. They're all booked in for operations at the end of the year."

And also injured were Sydney Roosters centre Billy Smith - a scorer in Sunday's NRL Grand Final - Wigan centre Jake Wardle, Leeds winger Ash Handley and prop Mikolaj Oledzki, who is leaving Headingley to join NRL side Perth Bears.

Grand Finalists Warrington have three players in the squad - Matty Ashton and Ben Currie joining captain Williams - while Wigan have seven, including Man of Steel winner Brad O'Neill and uncapped centre Zach Eckersley.

Mikey Lewis over Jake Connor feels like a call made based on pace rather than any other metric, as the Hull KR half is much more of a runner than his opposite number.

He's also perhaps more of an off-the-bench spark than the Leeds playmaker, given George Williams and Harry Smith's blend of run threat and game management will probably get the nod at six and seven.

Herbie Farnworth has been one of the best players in the world for some time and has taken his game to new levels in 2026, and getting the centre involved must be among Brian McDermott's biggest tactical challenges.

Dom Young is another thoroughbred who England will look to out wide, having helped Newcastle to the NRL Grand Final.

Victor Radley's influence and savage tackling makes him a shoo-in for the pack, something that was missed in last year's Ashes series against Australia, and there are other big hitters in the ranks with Morgan Knowles and Morgan Smithies also sharpened by their NRL exploits, and Brad O'Neill back in the international picture after a Man of Steel year.

Staying with the pack, the prospect of a Kai Pearce-Paul and Junior Nsemba second-row pairing whets the appetite.

Elsewhere, the new imports from the NRL have pedigree; Max King has played State of Origin, Hugo Savala can jump into a number of backs spots and Ben Talty is an athletic front-rower who helped Brisbane to success in 2025.

Zach Eckersley has impressed for Wigan this year, and his strong build and athleticism - coupled with an ability to put a winger away - make him a solid inclusion, while Matty Ashton's return after his missed the Ashes with an anterior cruciate knee ligament injury gives England genuine pace out wide.

Everyone will have their opinion on the squad, which features no selections from Super League champions Wakefield - albeit with some contenders unavailable - but there is a balance to the selection.

McDermott has said England might need something different to truly test the best, and it is that conundrum which will again be at the forefront of his thoughts.

Reece Walsh has secured a place in Australia's men's World Cup squad, also named on Monday - although head coach Kevin Walters has refused to confirm whether he will be first-choice full-back.

Walsh has struggled to hit the heights of last season, when he inspired Brisbane Broncos to their first NRL Grand Final triumph in 19 years before helping Australia to a 3-0 Test series win over England.

He missed the end of this season to have ankle surgery, but with Penrith's Dylan Edwards ruled out of the World Cup with a knee injury, Walsh will vie for the full-back spot with James Tedesco - man of the match as Sydney Roosters beat Newcastle Knights 19-18 in Sunday's NRL Grand Final.

Loose forward Isaah Yeo will delay surgery on a torn pectoral muscle to captain Australia.

Winger Mark Nawaqanitawase - who scored two tries in Sydney's win on Sunday - is not in the squad because of his impending code switch to union with Japanese side Saitama Wild Knights. Second-row forward Angus Crichton is absent for the same reason, as he is joining NSW Waratahs.

Star half-back Nathan Cleary is out of the tournament with a broken ankle.

Dual-code winger Nawaqanitawase stars as Roosters win NRL Final

Ali Brigginshaw has missed out on the chance to go for a fourth World Cup winners' medal after being omitted from Australia's women's squad.

Head coach Jess Skinner said the 36-year-old Brisbane half-back - Australia's captain when they won the tournament in Manchester four years ago - was "upset" to be left out.

"That was one of the hardest phone calls I've had to make as a coach to a player and to talk about her and where she was," Skinner said.

title: Liverpool will offload struggling forward: Three clubs want January deal
description: Liverpool strengthened their attack with a couple of new forwards in the summer transfer window. Victor Munoz was onboarded after the Reds triggered the FIFA World Cup winner’s £34m Osasuna release...
fullText:
Liverpool strengthened their attack with a couple of new forwards in the summer transfer window.

Victor Munoz was onboarded after the Reds triggered the FIFA World Cup winner's £34m Osasuna release clause.

And Andoni Iraola also reeled in Bradley Barcola in the closing stages of the window - with the France international arriving for a fee that could reach £123m.

Those signings will no doubt have an impact on forwards already on the books.

One such performer would be Federico Chiesa. The Italian, who turns 29 this month, finds himself well down the pecking order under Iraola this term.

Chiesa hasn't yet managed to make it into a single matchday squad under the Basque tactico having suffered an injury in a preseason friendly against Como.

Under contract until 2028 it has been speculated for a long time that the Euro 2020 winner would be heading back to Serie A. His wages - thought to be around £150k per week - are prohibitive for Italian sides while Liverpool are also insisting on a fee.

That has not stopped speculation ahead of the January transfer window however with three Italian top-flight sides now tracking Chiesa.

According to a report in Calciomercato Chiesa is wanted by champions Inter Milan as well as Lazio and Atalanta.

Describing Chiesa as a "struggling" Liverpool forward the report suggests that the versatile forward views a move back to Serie A as crucial to regaining his place in the national team.

"Federico Chiesa could return to Serie A during the winter transfer window, as the attacking winger continues to struggle to find a place at Liverpool," the report reads.

"Now in his third season in England, Federico Chiesa is ready to return to Serie A to try to find the consistency that could earn him a return to the national team in 2027.

"There are currently no concrete negotiations for the player, but Inter, Atalanta, and Lazio are closely monitoring the situation and could make an attempt for the former Juventus player during the winter transfer window."

Inter came close to landing Chiesa as an alternative to Luis Henrique during the summer window but ultimately the deal fell down.

Chiesa is currently miles off making it under Iraola - with younger players such as Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas now staking a claim for minutes on a more regular basis than the man signed in 2024 for £12.5m from Juventus.

title: Bowie seizing Scotland shot after World Cup disappointment
description: BBC Scotland speaks to Kieron Bowie after he scores his first goal for his country against North Macedonia.
fullText:
Sometimes, the solution to a problem can be hiding in plain sight.

On 19 May, Steve Clarke assembled his collection of players to embark on a World Cup journey.

Despite featuring and scoring for a Hellas Verona side heading for relegation from Serie A, and with a perennial problem of strikers not firing regularly for Scotland, Kieron Bowie was overlooked.

Given the loyalty Clarke showed to those who had served him so well, it was not a huge surprise. Neither was the impotence of the national team in the USA as they conjured up just one John McGinn goal.

"I received a message from him saying that I'm not in the squad but these things happen and it's just about how you bounce back from it to be honest," said Bowie.

"I scored goals in a struggling Verona team and that was as much as I could do. I was happy with where I was at and I was happy with how I'd played.

"I just spent a lot of time at home with my family and then a little golf holiday to Portugal for a week and that was all I did."

Two going on four, five or six on good night for new Scotland era

Scotland beat North Macedonia in Nations League for Pocognoli's first win

Bowie may have been cursing his luck again on Tuesday when his first international start was reduced to a mere 13 minutes following Jack Hendry's red card in the Hampden loss to Switzerland.

The landscape now looks very different.

The former Raith Rovers and Hibernian forward was one of the main Scotland heroes in Skopje after sending a deliciously whipped finish into the net in the 2-0 win over North Macedonia.

Playing in a new 3-4-1-2, Bowie started the game up top with Oli McBurnie in an ultra-attacking line up set out by Sebastien Pocognoli.

Throughout the game, his stats stacked up. The most shots with seven, the most on target with four, most shots in the box with five and the most touches in the opposition box with 11.

"You play all your life to represent a country and to score a goal is just an unbelievable feeling," said the 24-year-old Fifer.

"This manager's come in and he's put a lot of trust in me.

"I think the style that he wants to play definitely plays into my strengths. I think you've seen today a lot of times running them in behind and just showing strength against occupying defenders is one of the main things.

"It's a process but I think everyone's enjoying that process and it's a bit of a change."

The word "process" has been used so many times by the Scotland head coach and his players in recent days it's probably the new team motto.

Pocognoli is trying to implement a radically different system to his predecessor. Not only that, it's a different mindset. All while trying to embed a clutch of new players.

It's early days for the Belgian, his group, and, of course, Bowie. But the man on loan at Sassuolo believes things are clicking, and it's an opportunity for him to make his mark.

"It's a lot longer international break," he explained. "We spend a lot more time together so it's good for him to get his message across and his ideas. Also, we play more games so we have to train a little bit less of course.

"I think for me it's a fresh start with a new coach and different ideas.

"He said to me 'you don't need to prove yourself, just go and do what I know you can do' and I feel like I'm just doing that."

Bowie, who made his Rovers debut at 16, added: "I think people, obviously Scottish fans, have the same idea of how I was when I was at Hibs and that's all they can remember.

"But I feel like since I moved to Serie A, it's a different challenge against more experienced players and at a higher level.

"So, yeah, I feel like I've definitely kicked into another gear and I feel like I'm showing that."

title: Tuchel says rout in Rijeka can help heal England’s World Cup wounds
description: England boss Thomas Tuchel believes the 7-0 hammering of Croatia can help heal the wounds of the World Cup. Tuchel's side dismantled their familiar opponents in the Nations League clash in Rijeka, with a rampant front four of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Bukayo Saka and Anthony Gordon making hay.
fullText:
England boss Thomas Tuchel believes the 7-0 hammering of Croatia can help heal the wounds of the World Cup.

Tuchel's side dismantled their familiar opponents in the Nations League clash in Rijeka, with a rampant front four of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Bukayo Saka and Anthony Gordon making hay.

It was the sort of attacking performance that England fans were longing for in the summer, with the pain of the semi-final defeat to Argentina still raw.

But Tuchel said the manner of the display can point towards a brighter future as he said: "This is the only way to move forward, even if you still feel pain.

"You have to play with the pain if you still feel the disappointment, you have to play with it, that is the nature of sport.

"It was not an easy camp in the beginning after this long tournament for multiple reasons.

"But straight away, the first training session on Tuesday, the build-up to the Spain game, we had an excellent performance against Spain but not the result [losing 3-2], the reaction to the result in Czechia [winning 2-0] and now the build-up [here].

"The focus in the meetings, the translation of the meetings onto the pitch and to bring it within these circumstances in Croatia, to win with this dominant performance, that is the way to move on.

"I've said many times, we will always have a scar, we will always feel pain and disappointment. That is the way it is but this is the way to move forward.

"We adjusted some stuff after some things after the World Cup and we played in the same manner in all three matches. We are getting better at it and the team buys into it, this is the most important."

England were irresistible as they inflicted a biggest ever defeat on Croatia, described by Tuchel as a "complete" performance.

Kane and Saka both scored twice and got an assist, Bellingham notched one and made two others, while Gordon scored one and created another. Substitute Morgan Rogers added a late seventh.

Bellingham was the standout player with another virtuoso performance and Tuchel admitted: "At the moment, it seems like [he's gone to another level] and you always need to.

"The level you showed last week is never enough in the next week, that's just the nature of football.

"You can never stand still, If you stand still, it is like (being) on an escalator, If you walk against it, you have to walk to even maintain your level.

"You have to push for the next level, otherwise other teams will catch up. That's why it is always necessary to reach for the next level.

"It was a fantastic victory, the performance was on the highest level from the first to last minute.

"The hunger off the ball was the very highest level. I'm very happy about the attitude. We were never arrogant, always humble. It was a complete 90-minute performance."

Croatia are a far cry from the golden generation which saw them reach the 2018 World Cup final and semi-final four years later.

Slaven Bilic said: "I cannot offer any excuses. England were too good for us. We were not up to the level."

title: How Gordon became one of England's main men
description: Anthony Gordon has been England's in-form player since the World Cup knockout stage -  is the Barcelona forward now undroppable?
fullText:
Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Declan Rice, Jordan Pickford and now Anthony Gordon.

All have become guaranteed starters and reliable stars for England, with the Barcelona winger the latest to look, according to captain Kane, like one of the Three Lions' "main men".

Gordon was one of England's standout players at the World Cup and earned a big-money move to European giants Barca in the summer, while his good form has continued into his country's Nations League campaign.

He scored the opening goal in England's 2-0 win against the Czech Republic on Tuesday night, after also netting in a 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday.

In fact, the 25-year-old's England form has been building since the knockout stage of the World Cup began - his run of averaging a goal contribution every 69 minutes started with assisting both Kane's efforts in a 2-1 last-32 victory over DR Congo.

The former Newcastle player has scored three goals and provided three assists in his past six England matches, while he also won the penalty in England's dramatic last-16 victory over Mexico at Azteca Stadium.

And after a positive start in Spain, where he has already picked up five assists in La Liga, Gordon looks to be joining boss Thomas Tuchel's "undroppable" bracket.

Tuchel likes to give his players clarity on their role and makes clear who they are up against in the squad and for a starting position.

When asked whether Gordon is getting to be one of the first names on the team-sheet, he said: "He's getting there. He's defending his shirt, he's defending his position - an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain.

"He was very decisive [against the Czech Republic] and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult but the technique and finishing was excellent.

"He scored against Spain so he has decisive actions and he's defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he's a very important player."

Gordon linked up well with his former Newcastle team-mate Lewis Hall on England's left and combined with right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start for the Three Lions in nearly two years, for the opening goal.

Gordon said he had been "dying" to link up with Alexander-Arnold, who is also playing in Spain for Barcelona's rivals Real Madrid.

"It's a great compliment and it's great to play with him," Alexander-Arnold said of Gordon.

"I tried to get the ball, and try and see what the best play is and try and play forward and create something. And I was able to get the pass."

Captain and record goalscorer Kane is a guaranteed starter in England's biggest matches but the position to the left of Kane has been a problem area for the team, with no player able to make it their own.

Gordon looks to have secured that role and Kane said the winger is "showing that he belongs at the highest level, for Barcelona and England".

"His performances in the last couple of games have been some of his best that he has played in an England shirt," Kane said.

"I think he is just relishing putting the shirt on and being one of the main men in the team. He is an important player for us and he showed that during the World Cup."

It has not always been a straightforward route into the team for Gordon.

Marcus Rashford, Eberechi Eze, Phil Foden and Noni Madueke have all featured for England from the left in the past couple of years.

Gordon started to emerge as a clear option during Lee Carsley's time in interim charge, but said himself last October that he had only shown "50%" of what he can do for England.

Now that seems to be coming to fruition. Against the Czech Republic he attempted four shots, more than any England player and more than any of his team-mates against Spain too.

Gordon is ranked in at least the top four of England players for expected assists (0.9), expected goals (0.9), passes into the box (14), touches in the opposition box (29), chances created (eight), and shots on target (five), since the start of the World Cup knockout stage.

His importance is underlined by the fact he has contributed the same amount of goals and assists, six, as Bellingham since England faced DR Congo.

There has been an interesting subplot with Gordon and Rashford competing for a left-wing space for England and effectively Barcelona.

Rashford was on loan at Barcelona last season but they opted to not make his move permanent, instead he returned to Manchester United while the Catalan club splashed out £69m to sign Gordon from Newcastle.

Gordon has the ability to take on his full-back on the inside or beat them for pace on the outside before putting in a cross.

"People raised eyebrows when Anthony Gordon went to Barcelona for the money that he did and Marcus Rashford came back to Manchester United," former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"He has become a key part of the England team. There were certain games in the World Cup where he was substituted and he shouldn't have been - I think others should have come off instead of him.

"Gordon [when he is] full of confidence running at pace like he does, he can go either way and he's causing full-backs all kind of problems."

Gordon says that since his move to Spain he has changed people's perception of him being a player who is only quick and presses well, even if they are two of his best attributes.

"I always felt in England, people respected me because I was fast and I pressed but they never actually respected the quality and IQ that I play with," Gordon told ITV.

"Only the players I play with ever seem to notice that. I think now I'm at Barcelona and I play a different style, those qualities are highlighted much more and people are actually starting to take notice that I'm not just quick.

"In England, it was never really respected because people just see me as really quick and really aggressive.

"In Spain, they really appreciate my IQ and quality because at Barca, if you're not technical, if you're not smart, you're going to stand out like a sore thumb."

Tuchel is starting to build a team he thinks can challenge and win the Euros in 2028.

But first he wants to win the Nations League, and if England are to do that, it is likely Gordon will have played a huge part.

title: Wales wing Adams targets third World Cup
description: Wales wing Josh Adams is nearing full fitness in time for the autumn internationals and looking forward to a World Cup trip to Australia next year.
fullText:
Wales wing Josh Adams says he would love to play in a third World Cup as he targets a first trip to Australia next year.

It is exactly a year until Wales play their opening game against Zimbabwe in Adelaide on 2 October, before further pool games against Tonga and England.

"I'm desperate to go, but there is loads of rugby to be played and months ahead of us," said Adams, looking ahead to the tournament.

"It is important that you navigate your way through correctly and get to that start line in a good spot to be selected."

Adams, 31, was the World Cup's top try scorer in the 2019 tournament in Japan with seven as Wales reached the semi-finals.

The Cardiff back, who was also part of the squad that lost a quarter-final to Argentina four years later, insists he is just as excited for a hat-trick of global tournaments.

"I've never been to Australia, so that, as well as playing in a World Cup, is something I'm determined to do," said Adams.

Wales counting down the year until World Cup

The Warm Up: One Year To The Rugby World Cup!

Wales begin the World Cup countdown by playing four matches in the second half of the Nations Championship in November.

Japan, New Zealand and Australia will travel to play in Cardiff before a final play-off match at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham.

Adams was ruled out of Wales' 43-0 defeat by South Africa in Durban in July due to a calf injury.

The British and Irish Lions wing has missed Cardiff's start to the season but says he will be fit for international duty next month, with a club return expected in October.

"I am training, but it's important that you navigate your way through correctly and there's no rush," said Adams.

"I had the calf injury in the summer, but I've been good for a while.

"It's making sure that when I'm playing, I'm 100% fit and healthy, and I've had good preparation time."

title: Wales counting down the year until World Cup
description: With one year to go before the 2027 Rugby World Cup, what lies in wait for Steve Tandy's Wales over the next 12 months before they head to Australia?
fullText:
It might be hard to believe how quickly it comes around, but Thursday marks a year to go until the men's Rugby World Cup begins in Australia.

The 2027 competition starts on 1 October in Perth with a match between Australia and Hong Kong China, with the tournament finale on 13 November in Sydney.

Wales are to feature in the second game when they open their campaign against Zimbabwe in Adelaide on 2 October.

Steve Tandy's side sit 11th in the world rankings, currently topped by reigning World Cup champions South Africa.

The tournament has expanded from 20 to 24 teams, with the number of pools rising from four to six.

All 12 teams who finished inside the top three of their pools at the 2023 World Cup - France, New Zealand, Italy, Ireland, South Africa, Scotland, Wales, Fiji, Australia, England, Argentina and Japan - qualified automatically.

Georgia, Spain, Romania, Portugal, Tonga, Canada, United States of America, Uruguay, Chile, Zimbabwe, Hong Kong China and Samoa all earned their places through qualifying tournaments.

Wales have 12 or 13 potential matches across three blocks before they travel to Australia.

Nations Championship home matches are set to be staged against Japan, New Zealand and Australia in November, before a final play-off game at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium.

There will be five matches in the 2027 Six Nations, with trips to play France, Scotland and Italy and home fixtures in Cardiff against England and Ireland.

Following the end of the 2026-27 domestic season, Wales will meet up in the summer for fitness camps, with past trips including visits to Poland, Switzerland and Turkey.

There will be three or four World Cup warm-ups in the summer. The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has so far refused to publicly announce who they will face next August and September, or even how many games they will play.

The likely scenario is that Wales will play three games in Europe before a warm-up match on the way to or in Australia itself.

Tandy held alignment camps with more than 50 players in September, and the World Cup squad will eventually be whittled down to the final 33.

Wales have been drawn in Pool F alongside England, Tonga and Zimbabwe and will travel to play at three different venues.

The opening game against Zimbabwe will be staged in Adelaide, followed by a six-day turnaround before they face Tonga in Melbourne.

England await eight days later in Sydney on 16 October, before the expanded knockout stages.

Next year's World Cup will feature 16 teams at the knockout phase, rather than the traditional eight who previously went straight to the quarter-finals.

The top two teams from each of the six pools will progress to the last 16 alongside the four best third-place nations.

If Wales were to win their group, they would play the runner-up from pool B, which contains South Africa, Italy, Georgia and Romania.

Should Wales finish second, they would face the second-placed side in pool C, which is made up of Argentina, Fiji, Spain and Canada.

South Africa and New Zealand, World Cup finalists in 2023, are destined to meet in the quarter-finals, set to be staged in Sydney and Brisbane, if they top their groups.

The Olympic Stadium in Sydney will host both semi-finals and the bronze medal match, before staging the showpiece final on Saturday, 13 November.

title: Never played in Prem - and now face World Cup hosts
description: Jack Combes and Alex Post tell BBC Sport about a "dream come true" as they look ahead to the 2027 Rugby World Cup opener against hosts Australia.
fullText:
It is 1 October 2027. There are 61,000 fans inside Perth Stadium.

There is a global TV audience in the millions as two teams go through their final warm-ups preparing to open the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

For hosts Australia, twice world champions with a proud rugby history across the codes, it is familiar territory.

For their opponents Hong Kong China, it is anything but.

It will be their World Cup debut and for their players it will be biggest match of their lives.

Among them, all being well, are Jack Combes and Alex Post. Two players more used to the lower semi-professional tiers of the English league system than the global spotlight.

It is David v Goliath - in football parlance it is Spain v Cape Verde. You get the idea.

Twelve months earlier to the day, Jack and Alex are in Hong Kong. It is a national holiday and both have taken time out to tell BBC Sport about how their sporting and personal lives have been transformed.

"I think the whole run-up to the whole qualification process was already a dream in itself. To qualify for a men's first World Cup was huge," said Combes, a scrum-half.

There are glints in their eyes and smiles on their faces - why wouldn't there be?

Hong Kong China have been drawn in Pool A at the World Cup, where not just the hosts await, but also Chile - and the All Blacks.

"People will say it's daunting and it's a huge challenge to have those two top nations in your pool, but if you're going to do it, do it properly. Why not?" said Post.

"People might question whether we deserve to be there. But for me, if you asked anyone as a kid, if you could open up the World Cup in that first game in a year's time, it's genuinely amazing. A dream come true.

"And I'm sure anyone who does give us any criticism about us being there, there's no way they wouldn't be doing the same thing if they could, 100%."

Despite having made his international debut a decade ago, until recently Post was hooking for Richmond in The Champ.

"Unfortunately, I've never played at The Prem level. But The Champ definitely doesn't get the credit it deserves," said the 31-year-old.

"It's a very tough league. And that was great preparation for the international games."

Post was a full-time rugby player with Hong Kong China, before the Covid pandemic brought that to an end and he began a Masters degree at the University of Oxford.

The Varsity match at Twickenham remains one of the larger crowds he has played in front of.

"One of the unique selling points for Hong Kong is the players are contracted all year round and spend all their time together," said Post.

"So it wasn't really feasible for players like myself to stay at Richmond.

"Hong Kong was very much, 'we need boots on the ground'.

"I've moved my family and myself over the last couple of weeks and yeah, kind of chase the dream for the next year."

A full-time professional contract has enabled greater focus on the game away from being a financial analyst.

"With Richmond, we'd train twice a week and then you would do your own gym sessions in your own time," added Post.

"But you can probably do twice as much as that with Hong Kong now."

For Combes, 29, a former student and teacher at Hartpury College, it has been a circuitous route to professional sport that included a spell at Birmingham Moseley in England's third tier.

"So I've been full-time in the sevens for about three and a half years now," he said.

"I've done my career in reverse. I went from teaching after an ACL (anterior cruciate ligament injury), to playing semi-professional rugby, to being a full-time athlete at the age of 25.

"I wouldn't change it for the world, but going into a full-time environment where you have the resources, you have the training time, physical development, it's necessary for what we're facing."

Hong Kong has a proud tradition of rugby stretching back seven decades, not least around its annual sevens tournament.

They qualified for the World Cup by defeating Korea 70-22 in the final round of the Asia Rugby Championship last year.

A late 42-40 victory over fellow World Cup finalists Uruguay in July was perhaps the strongest showing yet of where they stand.

"The mindset's changed from years gone by where you compete in Asia and you play against teams that you know you probably should be beating," said Combes.

"Now we're completely on the other side of the spectrum where we've got nothing to lose.

"I think just be ambitious, be fearless, and go for it.

"'Be memorable' is the phrase that coaches have been talking about."

Both Post and Combes were born in Hong Kong and came up through the age-grade system there. They have witnessed how the game has grown there and are aware of the criticism they have faced, often focused on the international make-up of the team.

"It's always the first criticism we get after an international game," said Post.

"We don't go looking for that criticism or feedback. But it's always going to be there. I think for us, just perform and try and put something out there that people are proud of."

"I was born here in 1997," added Combes.

"Mum is half Chinese and going through the whole minis rugby here where we probably had one of the biggest mini rugby numbers base in the world, up until Covid.

"But I think the game's back growing within local schools - primary, secondary.

"Hopefully we can inspire the next generation."

Former London Irish and Ospreys director of rugby Toby Booth has joined the coaching set-up.

A good test of where they are at will come when Hong Kong China take on three countries in the Nations Cup next month, all with World Cup heritage, in the shape of USA, Canada and Tonga.

"Personally, I've got a whole bunch of pressure just from my family and friends," said Post.

"I've been getting messages all today saying it's one year, you better make the team.

"There will definitely be a big Hong Kong contingent [in Perth]. We want to be everyone's second team."

"You know, we are always going to be the underdogs," said Combes, who is known to his team-mates as Maradona for his keenness to kick any stray footballs that make their way on to the training pitch.

"I think our whole string of games leading into the World Cup with Nations Cup, warm-up games we're always going to be sort of looked over.

"But I think that works in our favour - we're just a bit fearless."

Oh, and remember Spain v Cape Verde at the Fifa World Cup? That ended in a draw.

title: England avoid Australia & India in World Cup draw
description: England avoid defending champions Australia and world number one-ranked side India in the group-stage draw for the 2027 ICC Cricket World Cup.
fullText:
England have avoided defending champions Australia and world number one-ranked side India in the group-stage draw for the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup.

India and Pakistan are, once again, placed in the same group, alongside Australia, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and a qualifier.

England, who won the trophy in 2019, are in the same group as co-hosts South Africa, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, New Zealand and a qualifier.

Harry Brook's side, who have enjoyed a resurgence in the 50-over format, begin their campaign against Bangladesh on 8 October, and Sri Lanka on 13 October in Windhoek, Namibia.

They will come up against South Africa in Gqeberha on 16 October before travelling to Harare to face a qualifier on 20 October. They round off the group stage when they face New Zealand, again in Gqeberha, on 23 October.

The visit to Zimbabwe is significant, with England having not played there since 2004.

Political unrest in Zimbabwe under the regime of former president Robert Mugabe caused problems for England's men's team throughout the 2000s.

England boycotted their fixture against Zimbabwe in Harare at the 2003 World Cup - a decision which ultimately derailed their campaign.

Relations have improved in recent years, however, and BBC Sport reported in 2025 that the two cricket boards were discussing a potential England tour of the country in the next cycle of international cricket between 2027 and 2031.

After three matches to decide the final two qualifiers, the tournament group stage will open with a repeat of the 2023 final when India and Australia face each other in Cape Town on 7 October.

Arch-rivals India and Pakistan, who do not play each other outside tournaments, will meet in Johannesburg on 10 October.

The top three, plus the best fourth-placed finisher, from the two groups progress to the Super 7 stage.

From there, the top four teams will qualify for the semi-finals, which are scheduled for 17 and 18 November, before the final on 21 November in Johannesburg.

title: World Cup-winning captain Stratford gives birth
description: Zoe Stratford, who captained England to World Cup glory a year ago, gives birth to a baby girl.
fullText:
England's World Cup-winning captain Zoe Stratford has given birth to her first child.

Stratford - nee Aldcroft - gave birth to a baby girl, who is currently nameless, on Wednesday.

England beat Canada in the World Cup final in September 2025.

Stratford, 29, joined Sale Sharks from Gloucester-Hartpury in the summer, having played a key role in their rise to become the dominant force in the women's domestic game.

Commenting on an Instagram, external post announcing the birth by Stratford's husband Luke, Sale said: "The most amazing news!"

Stratford was named World Player of the Year in 2021 and co-captained Gloucester-Hartpury to three back-to-back Premiership Women's Rugby titles.

She was the third England women's player to announce she was expecting this year, following Bristol's Lark Atkin-Davies and Abbie Ward.

In April England team-mates Marlie Packer and Rosie Galligan announced they are expecting a baby together, with lock Galligan due to give birth this month.

Meg Jones, who was named England captain after Stratford's pregnancy announcement, has recently called for England players to have access to fertility support and egg freezing.
