title: What will new call-ups bring to Northern Ireland?
description: Before the upcoming 2027 Women's World Cup play-off with Portugal, what will the five new faces bring to Northern Ireland?
fullText:
When Northern Ireland run out to take on Portugal in their 2027 Women's World Cup play-off, they know they will be the underdogs.

That would be the case even if Michael McArdle had a full-strength squad to pick from, but he has had to deal with a lengthy injury list before the first play-off round.

However, disappointment for some leads to opportunities for others, and his 23-strong squad as produced five new names.

Sparta Pargue forward Kess Elmore was a surprise inclusion but her versatility could be key, while Galway United defender Lucy-Jayne Grant is another new face.

McArdle has also rewarded three Women's Premiership players - Naomi McLaughlin, Jane McMaster and Charlotte Havern - with their first call-ups.

But what can they all bring to the international stage?

Elmore and Grant named in Northern Ireland squad

With the absence of key attackers Simone Magill, who is back in training after having her first child, and Danielle Maxwell and Caragh Hamilton, who are injured, the introduction of Elmore to the squad is intriguing.

The 27-year-old Sparta Prague attacker qualifies for Northern Ireland through her father, who is from Lisburn.

Elmore came through Liverpool's academy and made the move to the USA in 2017 to play college football for the UConn Huskies and Oregon Ducks.

Her professional career started with Saint Etienne in France in 2023 and moved to Brooklyn FC for the inaugural USL Super League the following year.

Elmore has Champions League experience with Austrian champions St Polten against the likes of Chelsea and Lyon, and she moved to the Czech Republic in July.

Predominantly an attacking midfielder, Elmore can play right across the forward line and McArdle says "that versatility brings a strength to us".

"The biggest thing for Kess is the attacking prowess she's got as a creative player and an attacking player," said the Scot.

"She's coming in with good experience of playing against high quality opposition, and Portugal's squad is full of players that are at elite European clubs.

"Not speaking on behalf of Kess, but when you get that first call up at the age of 27 it is quite a special moment.

"It's been quite a special few weeks working with Kess in the background, so I'm looking forward to her joining camp and bringing those qualities to the group."

As well as Elmore, another player who has earned their first call-up is Cavan-born left back Lucy-Jayne Grant, who qualifies for Northern Ireland through her father.

The 22-year-old plays for Galway United in the League of Ireland, and she helped the club win the cross-border All-Island Cup in 2024.

McArdle said he had identified Grant for a possible call-up early into this time at the job, and she had earned her chance after he and his staff done their "due diligence".

"Over the summer she's performed well and she has spent time in the environment as a training player, so we have got to know her.

"She has broken through now on the left side of defence, so she'll add to the depth within there with the squad."

As well as her on-pitch ability, Galway's website says that Grant can juggle and is a qualified piano and violin teacher, so should be able to entertain the camp throughout the window.

Women's Premiership players featuring in senior Northern Ireland squads is nothing new.

In fact, before the historic Euro 2022 finals, it was the norm.

While more players have moved to England or Scotland over the past few years, the Irish League still plays a key role for the international team.

In McArdle's squad for the play-off, eight of his players are still based in Northern Ireland, and he has handed three of them first call-ups.

Attacking midfielder McLaughlin, 20, broke through at Sion Swifts before she moved to Cliftonville in 2024.

Her performances at Solitude earned her a move to Aberdeen in January but she returned to Northern Ireland with Glentoran in July, where she has impressed.

"Naomi has had a real purple patch since returning to Glentoran," McArdle said.

"It is exciting for her. She gives us another attacking option and a bit of versatility because she's slightly different to some of the players that are in the squad."

Full back McMaster, 22, has been a stalwart at Linfield and has been a key player in the club's push into title contention this season.

McMaster, who can also play in the centre of defence, has represented Northern Ireland before both at underage level and with the futsal team, but this is her opportunity to win a first senior cap.

"Jane has had a few consistent seasons and come through the international pathway," said McArdle.

"She is having a fantastic season with Linfield and deserves her call-up, which is exciting."

At 16, Havern is the youngest players in McArdle's squad and has earned a call-up after helping Cliftonville to a Premiership and League Cup double, and the Reds are also in the Irish Cup final.

Another underage international, it will be a chance for McArdle to work with the all-action midfielder first hand in the senior squad.

"Charlotte's impressive form with Cliftonville and has been a key part of their performances this season.

"They have helped Charlotte break through into the national team to get this experience."

title: Fishlock set for Wales return - but not as player
description: Rhian Wilkinson says icon Jess Fishlock will be back with the national team if they reach a World Cup play-off final in December – but only as a coach.
fullText:
Rhian Wilkinson says in-form Wales icon Jess Fishlock will be back with the national team if they reach a Women's World Cup play-off final in December – but only as a coach.

Fishlock, Wales' most-capped footballer, called time on her international career last October.

But the 39-year-old continues to shine for Seattle Reign, having claimed two fine goals in last weekend's win over Boston Legacy to become the National Women's Soccer League club's all-time leading scorer.

Wales, meanwhile, are without a string of senior players for the World Cup play-off semi-final against Albania next month, but Wilkinson says she has turned down Fishlock's tongue-in-cheek offer to come out of international retirement.

"Jess could play forever, she's incredible," the Wales head coach said.

"There was never a doubt that Jess Fishlock could still do a job for us. [But] I think it was absolutely the right time for her to step away after that amazing qualification for the Euro [last year]."

Women's World Cup qualifying play-off semi-final

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales Extra, Radio Cymru, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Fishlock, who has said this will be her last year playing club football, will be on duty with Reign when Wales go to Albania on Friday, 9 October and then again in the return leg in Llanelli four days later.

Should Wales overcome a side who are 36 places in the Fifa rankings – and one they beat twice in the group phase of World Cup qualifying – they will play either Norway or Romania in a two-legged play-off final in December.

Wilkinson has revealed that another recently retired former player, Kayleigh Barton, will be part of her staff for the Albania ties and then Fishlock will have a role should Wales reach the final.

Fishlock previously worked as a technical assistant for Wales' opening game of this qualifying campaign, against the Czech Republic in March.

Wilkinson explained that Fishlock had been in touch before she named her semi-final squad on Tuesday, adding: "I didn't appreciate her saying 'call me up coach, I'm ready', which I thought was mean, but [she was] a wonderful player and a great leader for us.

"If we are able to get past Albania, she'll be coming in as a coach for us for the next round."

title: Young U.S. men's soccer team has ups and downs in 4-2 victory over Chile
description: But all in all, it was another good result and fun outing for a program returning from the World Cup with the second of four friendlies over 11 days.
fullText:
ST. LOUIS — Amid all the excitement about his young U.S. soccer team, a wide-eyed crew that started the new World Cup cycle with an enlightening performance over the weekend, Mauricio Pochettino warned there would be ups and downs along the way.

After all, almost half the roster had never played at the senior level and, as a whole, the group hadn't spent much time together.

Tuesday's 4-2 victory over Chile at bubbly Energizer Park reinforced the coach's admonition.

The gorgeous build-up on the first goal.

Sebastian Berhalter and Gio Reyna putting their stamp on another match.

Teenager Julian Hall's second goal in two appearances, and teenager Mathis Albert scoring his first.

Chris Richards' 72nd-minute tiebreaking goal as part of a second-half comeback.

All in all, it was another good result and fun outing for a program returning from the World Cup with the second of four friendlies over 11 days. For the second time in four days, the Americans scored four goals and flexed their muscles against a South American foe.

There were troubling moments, as well, particularly in the first half, when the Americans conceded numerous scoring opportunities and made many mistakes. They were fortunate to be tied at intermission.

But they showed resilience in the second half and, coupled with the 4-1 thumping of Peru last Saturday in Orlando, continued building momentum heading into this Saturday's showdown with rival Mexico in greater Phoenix. They will also play Canada on Oct. 6 in St. Paul, Minnesota.

In a pregame ceremony in his hometown, World Cup captain Tim Ream was honored for 16 years and 86 appearances with the national team. The Charlotte FC center back, who will turn 39 on Friday, announced moments earlier that he has retired from international soccer and won't weigh his club future until after the MLS season.

"The kids are getting younger and younger," he said. Ream was talking about the U.S. roster, not his own three kids.

"I actually got a text message last night [that] I was a senior at Saint Louis University when [17-year-old forward Cavan Sullivan] was born," Ream said. "I was like, 'He's only four years older than my oldest.'"

Ream was not selected to the current roster.

The starting lineup Tuesday averaged just over 23 years old, including teenagers Hall, Neil Pierre and Adri Mehmeti. The other young starters were midfielder Brooklyn Raines, 21, and right back Frankie Westfield, 20.

At almost 6-foot-7, the 18-year-old Pierre was unmistakable on the backline. Like Sullivan, he is enjoying a breakout club campaign with the Philadelphia Union.

Reyna was the only holdover starter from the Peru match. Like Saturday, Pochettino started six 2026 World Cup players: Reyna, Berhalter, goalkeeper Chris Brady, wingers Antonee Robinson and Sergiño Dest, and center back Miles Robinson.

Brady, 22, made his first international start after debuting as a sub in a World Cup tuneup.

Chile — which has missed three World Cups since winning the 2016 Copa America — was without captain Gabriel Suazo and Lucas Cepeda, La Liga-based players red-carded in the 1-0 loss to Canada on Saturday in Toronto.

As they did against Peru, the Americans threatened early off a Reyna set piece. His free kick from 25 yards met Miles Robinson for a point-blank header that Lawrence Vigouroux slapped aside in spectacular fashion.

The U.S. was organized and energetic at the start but not always precise. In the 18th minute, a miscommunication between Berhalter and Mehmeti led to a Chilean threat. A minute later, Berhalter's tasty through ball sent Hall in alone, but after rounding Vigouroux, his off-balanced, angled bid missed high and wide.

Brady was shaky, sitting back when he should've come forward and allowing Victor Méndez to test him. Then, on shots a minute apart, he also got lucky as Ben Brereton's screamer dinged the crossbar and Darío Osorio's low bid hit the far post.

Against the run of play, the match took an unforeseen turn.

Two minutes after Osorio's scare, the Americans went ahead in the 37th on a wonderfully constructed goal. They won the ball in midfield. Dest and Reyna played a sharp combination. With quick and clever footwork, Dest danced into the box. He crossed to Hall, who dummied the ball with the smarts of a veteran, allowing Berhalter to bury a 12-yarder into the far post.

Brady's problems continued. On the last act of the half — a Chilean corner kick — he punched the ball up, then backward. A mad scramble ensued. Finally, from inside the six-yard box, Diego Ulloa's side-volley caromed off Westfield's arm and into the net.

Brady's night — or nightmare — was over. As he did against Peru, Pochettino changed his goalkeeper at halftime: FC Cincinnati's Brian Schwake made his first appearance, becoming the 12th debut in this camp.

He couldn't do much about Maxi Gutiérrez's go-ahead goal in the 49th minute. Westfield's misstruck header in midfield allowed Gutiérrez to glide into the U.S. end. Berhalter failed to shut him down, and the Chilean forward whistled a 23-yard shot into the far corner with pinpoint accuracy.

Two minutes later, the U.S. answered. Reyna lifted a gentle cross into the box, where Hall rose from eight yards and headed it into the far side.

Pochettino turned to his bench and made seven subs, including five veterans. Vigouroux made a fine foot save on Antonee Robinson, but on the ensuing corner kick, Berhalter delivered a perfect ball to Richards for a powerful header from the edge of the six-yard box.

Chile threatened to pull even. The U.S. extended the lead on Albert's stab off the underside of the crossbar from close range. The announced crowd of 21,680 loved it.

Just before the final whistle, a benches-emptying scuffle broke out after a Chilean player tapped the fallen Schwake on the arm with his foot. Play resumed, but at the final whistle, another brief incident broke out.

"Take Me Home, Country Roads" boomed over the speakers.

Winger Cole Campbell, a first-time camper held out of the Peru match for an undisclosed ailment, and goalkeeper Diego Kochen, who played the second half Saturday, were not in uniform. Kochen was healthy, but Pochettino chose to dress 26 players again.

In his 60th appearance, Antonee Robinson captained the team for the first time.

Sullivan replaced Berhalter in the 83rd minute.

The Americans are 11-1-3 in greater St. Louis, including 5-0-0 at Energizer Park, which sits 1.3 miles directly west of the Gateway Arch and opened before the 2023 MLS season.

title: Yamal inspires Spain to Croatia romp on World Cup homecoming
description:
Lamine Yamal scored two goals and set up another as Spain hammered Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday in the Nations League in their first home game since lifting the World Cup. 
Captain Rodri showed off the World Cup trophy before kick-off at the packed Estadio Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan, being handed it by Sevilla legend Jesus Navas, a winner with Spain in 2010.
fullText:
Lamine Yamal scored two goals and set up another as Spain hammered Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday in the Nations League in their first home game since lifting the World Cup.

Yamal, 19, was joined on the scoresheet by Marc Pubill and Nico Williams as they extended their unbeaten run to 40 matches, which includes June's final triumph over Argentina in the United States.

La Roja next play Czech Republic on Saturday in Group A3.

Yamal's contribution strengthened his case for the Ballon d'Or, with voting having closed on Monday and the winner announced on October 26.

Captain Rodri showed off the World Cup trophy before kick-off at the packed Estadio Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan, being handed it by Sevilla legend Jesus Navas, a winner with Spain in 2010.

"We were very excited to bring the cup here," Yamal said.

"To be able to win the game and bring it home is great," he added.

Attackers Yamal, Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal started the game having scored in Saturday's thrilling 3-2 win over England at Wembley.

Croatia made six changes from the weekend's win over the Czech Republic, leaving icon Luka Modric on the bench.

Yamal opened the scoring within two minutes against the Three Lions and took just 75 seconds to do so against Slaven Bilic's side in Andalusia.

The teenager's left-footed finish took his tally of international goals to nine in 36 appearances.

Just before the half-hour mark, the visitors equalised through Dion Beljo's header as the 1.95m-tall attacker headed home from an Ivan Perisic cross.

Two minutes later the hosts restored their lead as Pubill fired home a header from a pin-point Yamal cross.

Just 45 seconds before the interval, the home side were denied a third goal by the post as Fermin Lopez failed to find the bottom corner.

Yamal claimed his second after 63 minutes, beating Barcelona team-mate and Croatia goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic at his near post, and with fewer than two minutes to play Athletic Bilbao's Williams notched up a fourth for Spain with a crisp dribble and finish.

title: Wales without seven players for World Cup play-off
description: Ceri Holland is one of seven players who will miss out through injury when a depleted Wales squad take on Albania in their Women's World Cup play-off semi-final next month.
fullText:
Ceri Holland is one of seven players who will miss out through injury when a depleted Wales squad take on Albania in their Women's World Cup play-off semi-final next month.

Influential midfielder Holland has not been included in the Wales squad having been sidelined for Liverpool's past three games.

Wales will also be without Olivia Clark, Hayley Ladd, Laura Hughes, Ffion Morgan, Ella Powell and Mia Ross due to fitness issues.

Head coach Rhian Wilkinson has handed first senior call-ups to two 18-year-olds, Newcastle United forward Casi Gregson and Tottenham Hotspur wide player Heidi Hills.

Wales travel to Albania for their play-off semi-final first leg on Friday, 9 October before the return in Llanelli four days later.

The winners will face either Norway or Romania in the play-off final in December.

Should Wales come through both play-off rounds, they may then have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs early next year to seal a place at next year's World Cup in Brazil.

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales Extra, Radio Cymru, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

The lowest-ranked of the eight play-off winners in Europe will go into the inter-confederation play-offs, and - should they get that far - there is a decent chance that would be Wales.

The loss of Holland for the Albania ties is a significant blow given her importance to Wilkinson's team, with the 28-year-old becoming arguably Wales' most important player since the retirement of Jess Fishlock in 2025.

The absence of Leicester City's Clark means Safia Middleton-Patel, who is on loan at Watford from Manchester United, is the only goalkeeper with any international experience in this Wales squad.

Crystal Palace player Ladd – who has 115 caps - Southampton midfielder Hughes and West Ham wide player Morgan could all have expected game-time in the Albania matches.

Ross, who is unattached after leaving Charlton Athletic earlier this month, and Bristol City's Powell both got minutes in Wales' most recent camp, when they drew in Montenegro and then beat the Czech Republic in June to seal top spot in their World Cup qualifying group.

Wales are unbeaten in their past eight internationals having endured a run of 12 games without a win which ended with a friendly success against Switzerland in December 2025.

title: Red Roses to return to Sunderland for Women's Six Nations
description: England will return to Sunderland's Stadium of Light – the venue for their record-breaking Women's Rugby World Cup opener – for the 2027 Six Nations.
fullText:
England will return to Sunderland's Stadium of Light - the venue for their record-breaking Women's Rugby World Cup opener - in their first home match of the 2027 Six Nations.

The Red Roses will play Scotland at the venue on 17 April.

It will be the first time they have played a home match away from a rugby-specific ground outside of a World Cup.

England drew 42,723 fans to the Stadium of Light for the 67-9 victory over the United States that opened the Women's Rugby World Cup in August 2025.

That attendance surpassed the 42,579 who watched the final of the previous edition as the Women's Rugby World Cup's biggest crowd.

The Red Roses subsequently smashed that mark again with an 81,885 sell-out for their final victory over Canada at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium.

England's 2027 Six Nations campaign also includes home matches against Italy at Northampton's DPD Stadium at Franklin's Gardens on 24 April and a final-round meeting against France at Twickenham on 15 May.

The venues for their away fixtures against Wales and Ireland are yet to be announced

"It was an amazing atmosphere to be a part of - one of the favourites in my career," England full-back Ellie Kildunne said of her previous visit to the Stadium of Light.

"I just remember the noise when we got off the bus and the amount of time the fans stayed behind afterwards. It was incredible. They really spurred us on that night.

"If the match with Scotland can replicate anything close to that night, it's sure to be another memorable occasion."

England are aiming for their ninth successive Six Nations crown.

Their preparations for the tournament will begin after they play two Tests against Canada and one Test against the United States on the away leg of their WXV Global Series campaign next month.

title: Top 14 award winner Willis reiterates desire to play Test rugby
description: Jack Willis, who last played for England at the 2023 Rugby World Cup,  retains his award as the best player in France.
fullText:
Jack Willis, who last played for England at the 2023 Rugby World Cup, jokingly challenged reporters to find him a way back into Test rugby after he retained his award as the best player in France.

Willis moved to Toulouse in November 2022 after Wasps went out of business, and was initially given dispensation to continue playing for England given the exceptional circumstances.

The back row won the most recent of his 14 caps in a pool-stage hammering of Chile, but, having opted to remain in French club rugby, has not been eligible for England since.

A long-standing policy restricts England selection to domestic-based players. It strengthens Prem clubs' ability to retain top talent, while England also benefit from increased access and control over their players.

Willis has been a huge success across the Channel. He was named player of the match in June's Top14 final win over Montpellier as he added a fourth French title to the Champions Cup crown he lifted in 2024.

Willis came top of a three-man shortlist for the Top14's best player for the 2025-26 campaign, seeing off competition from France and Bordeaux-Begles fly-half Matthieu Jalibert and Clermont-Auvergne's All Black Harry Plummer.

Willis becomes only the second player - after France captain Antoine Dupont - to retain the accolade.

The 29-year-old made his decision to stay at Toulouse, where his contract runs until 2029, despite knowing it would put him out of contention for an England spot.

"You know what you sacrifice," Willis said of his Test career.

"It's something I still want to do, but rules are rules."

Willis is now, in theory, available for selection by Ireland.

Three years have passed since he last appeared for England and, under World Rugby's 'birthright' rule, he could now represent a country which he, his parents or his grandparents were born in. Willis' grandfather was born in Belfast.

Ireland's strong preference for home-based players has been relaxed on rare occasions in the past with Jonny Sexton and Tommy Bowe continuing to play for their country despite moves to Racing 92 and the Ospreys respectively.

However, the likes of Simon Zebo have also found themselves excluded after heading overseas.

It is highly unlikely any compromise would be found that allows Willis to play for Ireland while remaining with Toulouse.

"I'm a quarter Irish, but they have the same rules as England," said Willis.

"You need to do some digging, that's your job, you find the way [around the rules]!"

title: Life bright for Gilmour after baseball and World Cup heartache
description: Scotland midfielder Billy Gilmour opens up on the pain of missing out of this summer's World Cup.
fullText:
Billy Gilmour sits at Lesser Hampden, a beaming smile bursting across his face.

The topic of conversation is revolving around him missing the World Cup in the summer, something that could have been defined by harrowing disappointment and regret.

Instead, the Napoli midfielder's face lights up when asked about a night at the baseball in Miami, where the injured Scotland ace was asked to hobble on to the field and hurl the ceremonial first pitch.

"I was nervous," Gilmour tells BBC Scotland, recollecting the evening at the Miami Marlins against the Texas Rangers.

"I was just so happy it wasn't a crap throw, or it was bouncing. It was some experience."

How Manzambi became one of Europe's best young talents

Listen: Can Scotland shock the Swiss at Hampden?

Pocognoli has no concern over Scotland's lack of goals

The maturity and level-headedness of the 25-year-old defies his years.

Just days before he was due to jet off to the United States with the Scotland squad for the first men's World Cup the nation had experienced since before he was born, a crushing blow.

In the farewell game at Hampden against Curacao, he suffered a knee injury that would mean he was left behind. While a body blow to Steve Clarke, his squad and the country, it would have been devastating to a young man with the world stage at his feet.

He admits those initial days were difficult as reality set in, but Gilmour seized the chance to become a supporter across Boston and Miami with his family around him.

"The boys fell on top of me and I've heard something straight away," he said of the injury. "Typical, try to run it off, make sure it was okay.

"It was tough. You have to take yourself away for a couple of days and I did.

"I got to go away for a bit, just kind of switch off and it happened, so I had to deal with it. When you're there around the squad, you try to be as best as you can, as positive as you can.

"When you think of it, how lucky you still are to get to go there and watch the games and be with family and family holiday also."

Gilmour added: "I would be with the team some nights, but the squad and Robbo [captain Andy Robertson] and the gaffer, Steve Clarke, at the time, he basically said: 'Look, if it's too much to come in, don't come in. Stay as much time with the family. Go and experience it with the fans'."

Gilmour was still in Miami when news broke of Clarke's resignation as Scotland head coach. He's a man the Napoli midfielder acknowledges he owes so much to after giving him his debut in 2001.

Now, however, it's the Sebastien Pocognoli era and the former Rangers, Chelsea and Brighton & Hove Albion man seems central to it.

In the 0-0 draw in Slovenia on Saturday, it was Gilmour who caught the attention during a resurgent second half for the Scots.

He is often seen as more of a deep-lying central midfielder, but there was a different dynamic to his game with the absence of club-mate Scott McTominay, who is recovering from a heart procedure.

"When I was younger, I really liked playing higher up, trying to be among it," Gilmour, who is set to feature at Hampden on Tuesday against Switzerland - live on the BBC, said.

"Whenever I get asked to play on the pitch, as long as I'm on the pitch, I'm happy. I just want to play football and enjoy it."

Now 25, there is plenty time to make new memories in a Scotland shirt. Yet, with so many young faces coming into the squad, the Ayrshire man is probably now a senior figure in the group.

It's something he says he embraces, although Gilmour is coy about the prospect of maybe taking on the armband whenever current captain Robertson decides to pass it on.

"For me, it's everyone's dream to be a captain at a club or a country," he said.

"Of course I'd be really proud to, but Robbo's my captain and he's a really good captain as well.

"What he's done for Scotland is incredible and he's very close on the record [most caps held by Kenny Dalglish] and I'm sure he'll get it."

The Lionesses face Greece in their Women's World Cup qualifying play-off matches in October.

title: Australia-born Strange in England World Cup squad
description: Australia-born second-row forward Jasmin Strange is one of four potential debutants in England's 23-strong squad for the World Cup.
fullText:
Australia-born Jasmin Strange is one of four potential debutants in England's 23-strong squad for the World Cup.

Sydney Roosters second-row forward Strange, who is set to play in Sunday's NRLW Grand Final against Brisbane Broncos, has committed herself to England, for whom she qualifies through her mother Adele.

The 23-year-old is the daughter of Roosters women's head coach John Strange, who played for Featherstone in the 1990s.

Strange is joined by three uncapped players - Leeds Rhinos' Connie Boyd, Hope Millard of Canterbury Bulldogs, and Wigan Warriors' Lucie Sams.

In addition to Strange and Millard, whose father Shane was a forward for Widnes, Leeds and Wigan, three other NRLW players have made the squad - including dual code international Fran Goldthorp, who last played rugby league for her country at the most recent World Cup in 2022.

Newcastle Knights' Georgia Roche and Hollie-Mae Dodd of Canberra Raiders have also been included.

Strange's inclusion as a heritage player - one who qualifies through parentage - comes after eligibility rules were relaxed this year.

An International Rugby League ruling means that players can now represent more than one of the three tier one nations - Australia, New Zealand and England.

That led to speculation that head coach Stu Barrow might call on more heritage players with NRLW experience - such as Roosters playmaker Jocelyn Kelleher, Bulldogs half-back Tayla Preston and Wests Tigers full-back Caitlin Turnbull.

But Barrow has said he wants to give homegrown players an opportunity to develop.

All three Woman of Steel nominees - Jenna Foubister, Eva Hunter and Megan Williams - have been selected, along with six of their Wigan team-mates. Grand Final winners York Valkyrie have one player in the squad in forward Liv Wood.

Loose forward Jodie Cunningham, who will retire after the World Cup, is selected along with St Helens team-mate Vicky Whitfield, who will be competing at her fourth World Cup.

Barrow said: "Narrowing our squad from 40 players to a final 23 has involved some difficult decisions, but we believe we have the right balance of experience and youth to compete on the world stage.

"It's also an exciting moment for the programme with the inclusion of Australian-based heritage players for the first time."

This year's men's, women's and wheelchair World Cups will run concurrently, with England competing in all three. The wheelchair squad was announced last week, while the men's squad will be confirmed on 5 October.

The tournaments are being staged largely in Australia, with Papua New Guinea's men and women each playing two pool matches in their own country, and their New Zealand counterparts playing one.

England face three group matches - beginning in Perth against Wales on 17 October and Australia on 24 October, before facing Samoa in Wollongong on 30 October.

The top two sides in England's four-team group will go through to the semi-finals on 7 and 8 November, with the final on 15 November.

title: Newcastle agree delay to Fineanganofo arrival
description: Free-scoring All Blacks wing Fehi Fineanganofo convinces Newcastle Red Bulls to delay his arrival on Tyneside so he can chase his dream of playing at the Rugby World Cup.
fullText:
Free-scoring All Blacks wing Fehi Fineanganofo has convinced Newcastle Red Bulls to delay his arrival on Tyneside so he can chase his dream of playing at the Rugby World Cup.

It was originally announced back in January that the 24-year-old had agreed a two-year deal with Newcastle, beginning at the start of the current campaign.

However, Fineanganofo's exceptional form with the Wellington-based Hurricanes in Super Rugby then propelled him into Test reckoning.

He made his New Zealand debut against France in July.

Under All Blacks selection rules, a move overseas this year would have put Fineanganofo's emerging international career on ice and ruled him out of contention for the Rugby World Cup, which begins in October 2027.

Newcastle have therefore allowed Fineanganofo to stay with the Hurricanes, for whom he broke the record for the most tries in a single Super Rugby campaign this year, for an extra season.

His Newcastle deal is still for two campaigns, but now covers the 2027-28 and 2028-29 seasons instead.

"I'm really grateful to Newcastle Red Bulls for the support and understanding they've shown me," said Fineanganofo.

"The opportunity to stay in New Zealand and push for selection for the Rugby World Cup means a huge amount, and I'm fully committed to joining the club after the tournament and giving everything I can to the team."

Newcastle's sporting general manager Neil McIlroy said: "We are fully supportive of Fehi's desire to represent his country at Rugby World Cup 2027, which marries with our own philosophy of aiming high and enabling our athletes to achieve their ambitions.

"Fehi's arrival in 2027, with additional international experience that will only add to his already devastating qualities as a top-class winger, is another statement of intent around where this club is going."

The compromise ends long-running uncertainty about Fineanganofo's future.

In June, New Zealand Rugby denied they were attempting to put together a deal to get Fineanganofo out of his Newcastle contract.

Just a few weeks ago, Red Bulls' head coach Dan McFarland said he expected Fineanganofo to arrive in November and play in the current campaign.

His side began the Prem season with former Ulster man Werner Kok, signed in June as doubts over Fineanganofo's move increased, and 35-year-old Christian Wade as their first-choice wings.

McIlroy kept open the possibility of adding to the club's options in that position.

"We are more than happy with the quality and depth that our existing squad possesses, but may yet choose to add to the outside back position if a player of the required standard becomes available," he said.

Newcastle lost 59-26 away to defending champions Northampton on Friday in their league opener, and will take on Leicester at home on Saturday.

title: Yesterday sucked... I'll be back, says Cleary
description: Nathan Cleary responds to the horrific injury that has ruled him out of the Rugby League World Cup by promising "I'll be back."
fullText:
Nathan Cleary has responded to the horrific ankle injury that has ruled him out of the Rugby League World Cup by declaring "I'll be back."

The Australia great, 28, will miss the tournament in his home country after suffering a compound fracture and dislocation to his left ankle while playing for Penrith Panthers in their NRL play-off defeat by Newcastle Knights on Sunday.

Half-back Cleary - who helped Australia win the World Cup in Manchester four years ago - needed emergency surgery in hospital after being injured in a tackle by Phoenix Crossland.

Knights hooker Crossland was sent off for a 'hip-drop' tackle - which the NRL outlawed in 2020.

A hip-drop tackle is committed when a defender grabs the runner with both hands or wraps them with both arms, and then swivels or drops the hips or lower body, landing on and trapping the opponent's leg below the knees.

"Surgery done... Thank you so much to everyone that has reached out, the support has been unbelievable," Cleary posted on Instagram.

"Yesterday sucked but it's all part of the journey and it's made me even more grateful for the people I have around me. I'll be back."

Cleary had started Sunday's match on the bench because he was already carrying an injury to his right foot, which had a broken bone.

His father Ivan, the Panthers' head coach, said afterwards that his son would have surgery on both feet.

"I think that's why I was even more emotional on what happened to him, how hard he worked and what he put himself through to get himself to play today," the coach said.

Crossland was referred to the NRL Judiciary over the tackle, and is likely to receive a lengthy ban which would not only rule him out of Sunday's NRL Grand Final, in which Newcastle face Sydney Roosters, but may also affect his availability for New Zealand during the World Cup.

Australia will face New Zealand in the opening match of the World Cup in Sydney on 15 October (10:05 BST). The two teams are also favourites to face each other in the final, in Brisbane on 15 November (08:35 GMT).

title: NI qualifying for World Cup 'surreal' - O'Hanlon
description: Northern Ireland netball vice-captain Caroline O'Hanlon says "not many outside of our camp expected us to qualify" after the booked their spot in the 2027 World Cup in Australia.
fullText:
Northern Ireland netball vice-captain Caroline O'Hanlon said "not many outside of our camp expected us to qualify" after the side booked their spot for the 2027 World Cup in Australia.

Sheonah Forbes' side secured their place in Sydney after beating Wales and the Republic of Ireland during their impressive qualifying campaign in East Kilbride.

It will be the first World Cup for Northern Ireland since 2019, after they missed out on the 2023 edition in Cape Town.

"There wouldn't have been many outside of our camp who expected us to qualify," O'Hanlon told BBC Sport NI.

"It's so exciting, even since Friday, we've been inundated with well wishes and messages from home and people watching the games on BBC. It's been brilliant to have that exposure.

"It just seems surreal. We've been training away and we knew we had that potential, but obviously potential is one thing, getting it over the lines is a different thing and I am so proud of the group that we were able to get it over the line."

World-ranked number 15 Northern Ireland's emphatic 73-50 victory over Republic of Ireland in their final qualifier was not enough to secure one of the two qualification spots automatically.

However, Scotland's narrow win over Wales in Sunday's later game booked both teams spots with Wales, who are ranked ninth in the world, missing out.

"It was a real rollercoaster of a day," O'Hanlon continued.

"Obviously we started out with a hard-fought win against the Republic of Ireland, but we knew that we were still relying on Scotland.

"That match was just up and down the whole way through, so we were nerve-wrecked watching that. Just sitting in the stands, not being able to control anything, was nerve-wracking."

O'Hanlon was captain of the side when they finished 10th in the World Cup seven years ago.

But, now, the 31-year-old said the squad will head to Sydney with ambitions of competing for results rather than simply gaining experience.

title: Explained: Why Cricket West Indies slashed player salaries by 25%, suspended Super50, & what it means for 2027 World Cup
description: Why did Cricket West Indies slash player retainers by 25% and suspend the Super50? We explain the Caribbean cash crisis and its impact on the 2027 World Cup.
fullText:
Explained: Why Cricket West Indies slashed player salaries by 25%, suspended Super50, & what it means for 2027 World Cup originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Cricket West Indies has slashed international retainer fees by 25 per cent while shifting domestic players onto shorter seven-month contracts.

The board has suspended this year's men's Super50 and women's T20 Blaze tournaments, citing unsustainable operational and travel costs across the region.

CWI is redirecting its focus and resources toward preparing the men's ODI squad for the crucial 2027 World Cup qualifier campaign.

Cricket West Indies has pulled the trigger on an overhaul of its finances and domestic structure, and has rolled out a package of cost-cutting measures the board says is meant to tackle a deepening financial, developmental and competitive crunch.

International players will keep their 12-month contracts, but the money attached to them is shrinking by 25 per cent. Domestic cricketers face an even bigger structural shift, moving from full-year deals down to seven-month retainer contracts instead. Given how many West Indies players already lean toward franchise leagues over central contracts, this cut risks accelerating that trend rather than slowing it down.

CWI chief executive Chris Dehring is framing the pay cut as a reluctant but necessary call. However, before getting into the specifics, he acknowledged the players' side had cooperated through a difficult process.

"International retainer contracts will remain at 12 months but there will be a 25% reduction on the retainer fees," he said.

"We appreciate the spirit of cooperation of the West Indies Players Association and the players who have demonstrated their total understanding of the circumstances we all face. While not ideal, it is a necessary step towards financial stability."

MORE: 'Time to measure up': Daren Sammy issues rallying cry ahead of IND vs WI ODIs to end West Indies' 24-year series drought

CWI confirmed that this year's men's Super50 and women's T20 Blaze tournaments won't go ahead, and pointed to the sheer cost of running domestic competitions across a region spread over multiple independent nations.

That's a significant blow to the traditional route into the men's ODI team, especially with West Indies staring down a World Cup qualifier in February-March 2027 after already missing the 2023 edition of the tournament.

MORE: Rohit, Virat back in action: Gill-led India to assemble in Thiruvananthapuram for WI ODIs

Dehring didn't mince words when explaining just how unsustainable the current model had become, walking through the financial reality before laying out the raw numbers.

"Our domestic tournaments as structured historically, where Cricket West Indies bears the entire cost of every national team and tournament - whether it is age-group, development or senior for both men and women - including salaries, match fees, airfares, hotels and event staging costs, are simply unsustainable," he said.

"The high cost of domestic travel and accommodation absorbs too much of our scarce resources every year instead of being deployed for the direct benefit of our cricket."

He then pointed to a massive figure that's been quietly draining the board's coffers for over a decade, which shows just how one-sided the arrangement with domestic airlines has been:

"Indeed, over eighty million US dollars has been spent by Cricket West Indies with domestic airlines over the past 15 years, without receiving a dollar of sponsorship from those beneficiaries," he added.

"We must also deal with the immediate cash crunch brought about by years of bearing this burden and the crippling financial losses that emanate as a result."

MORE: Shamar Joseph gestures to Kieron Pollard to 'shut up' in apparent disrespect before wild celebration to WI legend's dismissal

With the domestic calendar trimmed back, CWI will now focus on preparing the men's ODI squad for 2027 ODI Qualifiers.

A string of white-ball fixtures against a touring England A side in November will lead into a dedicated ODI team camp, which will give the squad the best possible pathway to get ready for February's qualifiers.

However, amid the cash crunch, the ICC had sanctioned a loan to the board, but the terms and conditions are proving to be a hindrance.

"In July of this year the ICC approved a loan facility to Cricket West Indies totaling US$16 million to provide temporary relief to our chronic cashflow challenge, available in 3 tranches over the next year," the statement said.

"As with any other lender, this loan comes with terms of repayment and conditions that will require Cricket West Indies to attain critical metrics in order to access those funds starting this month."

MORE: 'Next Andre Russell': Former RCB analyst introduces WI cricket's next Dre Russ

This restructuring lands at an awkward moment too, with West Indies cricket's unusual multi-nation setup now facing fresh demands ahead of the 2027 Pan American Games in Lima and the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

The top four sides from the 2025-26 Super50 and T20 Blaze editions have already locked in their Pan American Games spots, but with those tournaments now suspended, CWI has unveiled replacement invitational events for Olympic qualification instead.

Dehring laid out how this new invitational structure is meant to work, framing it as a chance for individual nations to take ownership of their Olympic ambitions.

"These replacement tournaments will be by invitation to the 10 countries under the aegis of Cricket West Indies that qualify for Olympic participation," he said.

"We are excited by these new invitational tournaments...It's an opportunity for individual countries to galvanize national resources to chase Olympic glory, with the responsibility and cost of participation falling on their respective national cricket and Olympic associations, private sectors, governments and people. The winners of those tournaments will qualify for the ICC Olympic Qualifying tournaments for a spot in Los Angeles in 2028."

There's no sugar-coating this: an $80 million airline bill over 15 years with nothing coming back in sponsorship is the kind of number that demands drastic action, and Dehring deserves some credit for laying the figures out instead of burying them.

But the timing couldn't be worse. Cutting pay just as franchise leagues keep poaching West Indies talent risks pushing more players away from the international setup altogether, right when the team needs its best players available for a qualifier campaign that could decide whether they even make the 2027 World Cup.

Moreover, suspending Super50 also guts the one domestic tournament that's actually produced proven ODI performers in recent years. The decision to push the financial burden of Olympic qualification onto individual boards might work in theory, but smaller nations within the West Indies structure simply don't have the private-sector or government backing to make that work evenly. This is survival mode, not a growth strategy, and West Indies cricket can't afford many more rounds of it.

title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner
description: Martyn Jackson never thought he'd play football again when he had a heart transplant in 2024. Less than two years later, he was a World Cup winner with England.
fullText:
When Martyn Jackson walked off the pitch after Ramsbottom United's 2-1 win over Cheadle Town in October 2024, it never crossed his mind that one day he could be a World Cup winner.

In fact, in the days after that match, his goal was just staying alive.

Just a couple of days after the final whistle, Jackson started to feel unwell during the night.

He went into hospital and was diagnosed with myocarditis, an inflammation of the heart usually caused by an infection. Within weeks, he was placed on the super urgent waiting list for a transplant.

His life was saved when a donor heart became available, and on 28 November 2024, he had successful surgery at Wythenshawe Hospital in Greater Manchester.

Fast forward to September 2026, and Jackson scored for England in their 5-1 win over Spain in the final of the Transplant Football World Cup.

His team-mates and opponents were, like him, all recipients of a donor organ.

"Obviously, when you've had a transplant, you don't think you're ever going to play again. That's what I thought anyway," Jackson tells BBC Sport.

"I'll be forever grateful to my donor and the family for what they've given me. They've given me the gift of life and the opportunity to live my life to the fullest."

Football at the Transplant World Cup is not quite the same as the game played at the Fifa World Cup.

Instead, it reflects how delicate each player's body is having been through life-altering surgery.

Matches are seven-a-side and played over 20-minute halves. Contact is "not as aggressive as I was used to", Jackson says.

Having played 11-a-side football in the ninth tier of English football before his surgery, he became a game-changing new addition to the national transplant team when he joined up with the squad in January 2026.

Jackson spent his youth career in the academy at Manchester United, before spells at Blackburn Rovers, Preston North End and Burnley. He eventually stopped pursuing a career as a professional and spent 13 years with clubs across the non-league pyramid.

During his recovery, wife Lucy heard about the opportunity to join an England Transplant FC team on social media.

Daley Cross, manager of the England team, said of Lucy's role: "She was just trying to do her best for him and trying to find a way to motivate him.

"His wife did drop in the conversation that he used to play at Manchester United as a schoolboy. So that got our ears twitched instantly.

"You could tell from him being on the pitch, even though he was so fresh into his journey, that he knew the football game and he would be such an incredible asset to us.

"You can be in a dark place, at the time of diagnosis, through your treatment or even post-transplant. So to have us exist to help and inspire people means that we are getting some incredible footballers.

"And that really is the power of it: to that transplant community or to the world, showing people that when you've had organ failure, your life isn't over. There is a chance for you, and you can go and resume and live your life."

As the recipient of a donor heart, Jackson has to manage his exercise workload more carefully than his team-mates, many of whom have had kidney transplants, the most common transplant in the UK.

His role in the side tends to involve 10-minute bursts, rather than playing for the duration of matches.

Bayern Munich's Alphonso Davies was diagnosed with a mild form of myocarditis in 2022. He was sidelined for nearly five months, undergoing specialist cardiac monitoring, before returning to play.

Jackson started to feel ill two days after Ramsbottom side's win over Cheadle, and his case became so severe that doctors had to fit his heart with a mechanical pump to keep him alive.

"Of course it was extremely scary," he says, "but at that stage, when you are critically ill, there's not really much you can do about it. You have to accept it."

The super urgent waiting list he was placed on is the highest priority of the three tiers of patients waiting for a new heart. Typically, only about four or five people are on the list at any one time in the UK.

Dr Paul Callan, a consultant cardiologist at Wythenshawe Hospital's Heart and Lung Centre, worked with Jackson during his diagnosis and recovery.

"Initially, we used to quote an average wait of seven days on the urgent transplant list," he says. "Now it's up to 14 days. Maybe 10% of patients who are put on the list get too poorly and have to be taken off the list."

That increased waiting time is the result of a reduction in the numbers of organ donors in the UK, with a 9% drop recorded in 2026 compared to the same period last year. There are 8,700 people currently waiting for a donor organ, a figure that NHS Blood and Transplant say is an all-time high.

This Organ Donation Week,, external which runs from 21-28 September, the NHS has launched an urgent response plan to address the decline.

Jackson has yet to meet the family of the donor from which he received his new heart. He says he is considering reaching out to them around the two-year anniversary of his surgery.

For him to make a recovery within that time frame, culminating in playing football in a Transplant World Cup, is "remarkable", according to Dr Callan.

England beat six teams on their way to winning last Friday's final in Frankfurt, scoring 36 goals, but for every player at the tournament there is gratitude that they even have the opportunity to play a football match again.

"It is so important to spread that message, have that conversation about organ donation," says England manager Cross, "because our team only exists for that reason.

"I wouldn't have 16 players to manage if we didn't have organ donation. And England wouldn't have just gone and won a World Cup."

title: Ronaldo spurred on by 1,000 goals and Portugal glory
description: Cristiano Ronaldo contemplated retirement after the World Cup but wants to reach 1,000 career goals and help a new-look Portugal thrive before hanging up his boots.
fullText:
Cristiano Ronaldo considered retiring after the World Cup but says he opted to extend his glittering career as he believes he can help Portugal to further success - and reach a personal milestone of 1,000 career goals.

The 41-year-old confirmed in the summer that the 2026 World Cup would be his last, although his long-term future remained uncertain.

However, he has been included in Jorge Jesus' 25-man squad for Portugal's Nations League campaign, which begins against Wales in Lisbon on Thursday night.

In the lead-up to the contest with Craig Bellamy's side, the Al-Nassr forward also targeted the 21 goals needed to reach that magical 1,000 mark.

Asked if he thought about retiring from international duty after the World Cup, Ronaldo responded: "Yes, I did.

"Of course, I'm always thinking on my decisions, my future, the present also. I'm a thinker, you have to think."

The former Sporting, Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus player said: "I had a conversation with our president, with our coach. I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to reach what they want.

"I think I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football."

Ronaldo is a two-time Nations League winner with Portugal, and he said adding a third title was also an aim alongside his personal ambitions.

"Both aims are important," he said.

"One thousand goals, yes, and the national team. Winning the Nations League, the competition starts tomorrow [Thursday], it's a new age."

Young talents including Fabio Silva, Renato Veiga, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves and Francisco Conceicao all feature in Portugal's squad for this international window.

Ronaldo - who joked he will play on for another decade - says helping his country's newest talents was also a pivotal factor in his decision to continue to represent Portugal.

"This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games," he said.

"For me, the most important thing, I know what I am. I know what I do to be here, to have the success that I have.

"I know why young kids love Cristiano, because they see me as an example, and I will continue to do that. Even when I am retired... in 10 years!

"I'm happy with myself. It doesn't matter if I play tomorrow, if I rest the next game. For me, the most important thing is that I feel good."

It came after the five-time Ballon d'Or winner addressed the criticism he has faced throughout his career - particularly during his time with some of the great clubs of England, Spain and Italy.

"This [Portugal] is possibly where I have felt most cared," Ronaldo said. "From the fans, I also feel the Portuguese like me.

"I do understand that some TV channels like to criticise me, they've tried to kill me with a shotgun, but I can still move away from it.

"Anyway, I am used to it. For over 20 years I have been doing this, but my memories are with people who love me."

title: England players carrying World Cup scar - Saka
description: England winger Bukayo Saka says the team are still carrying the "scar" of their heartbreaking World Cup semi-final exit to Argentina.
fullText:
England winger Bukayo Saka says the team are still carrying the "scar" of their heartbreaking World Cup semi-final exit to Argentina.

Thomas Tuchel's team were on the verge of becoming the first England side to reach a men's World Cup final since 1966, but were stunned by two late Argentina goals as they fell to a 2-1 loss.

A thrilling 6-4 victory over France in the bronze medal match gave the Three Lions their best World Cup finish in six decades, but the wait for their second trophy goes on.

"Obviously, there is still a scar on us when you believed and everyone was so united and so confident we could do it," Saka said.

"Not just us, but the whole country we felt.

"You try to move on as soon as possible, but you know a scar is a scar, it decides to heal when it heals itself."

England get an immediate reminder of what might have been as they host world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday (19:45 BST) in the first of four Nations League matches over the next two weeks.

"We are trying to draw a line under [the World Cup] now and focus on the new international season that we have coming up," Saka added.

"We have got four massive, difficult group games to try and qualify us for the Nations League [knockouts] that we are really focused on."

Meanwhile, Saka believes it is only a matter of time before his Arsenal team-mate Max Dowman, 16, earns a senior England call-up.

"I think so," Saka said. "His talent is insane. It's up to him how far he is going to go in football. His talent is crazy."

England Under-21 manager Lee Carsley concurred with Saka on Dowman's "amazing talent" but thinks the youngster staying with the under-19s during this international window is the best option.

"He is more than capable of playing in the under-21s," Carsley said.

"What I do think will happen with the age group he goes to is that he can play the minutes.

"He can also have that time to consolidate where he is in his career and play with his friends again and take that little bit of pressure off him.

"I have no doubt that Max is going to be with the under-21s.

"That is something I am keen to have a conversation with him and his parents, on the way we see his pathway going, because he is an amazing talent and someone we are very lucky to have."

title: Wales pick two father-son duos for Wheelchair World Cup squad
description: Fathers and sons Martin and Matthew Turner and Gareth Ramsey and Sid Ramsey are named in Wales' squad for the 2026 Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup.
fullText:
Wales have named two pairs of fathers and sons - Martin and Matthew Turner and Gareth and Sid Ramsey - in their squad for the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup in Australia.

It is the first time a father and son have represented Wales together at a Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup and the first time two such pairings have been named in one squad.

A father-and-son pair have featured in the Wales set-up previously, but never before on the World Cup stage.

Head coach Alan Caron included them in his 12-strong selection for the tournament, which starts for Wales against England on Friday, 30 October in Wollongong.

Group games against Ireland and the United States follow at the same venue as the teams aim for the knockout stages.

Gareth Ramsey, John Berriman and Fionn McCabe - who turns 16 shortly before the competition - could make Wales debuts during the event.

Caron said: "Having two father-and-son combinations in the squad makes this World Cup particularly special.

"Gareth and Sid, and Martin and Matthew, have the opportunity to share something that very few players ever get to experience: representing Wales together at a World Cup.

"For John, Fionn and Gareth, the opportunity to make their Wales debuts at a World Cup would be something very special, while our experienced players will be vital in helping them and the rest of the squad through the tournament."

Wales have had to fundraise to help with the costs of taking the squad to Australia, with more than half of the £10,000 target donated so far.

title: Scots recall Kerr & Thomas for World Cup play-offs
description: Sam Kerr and Martha Thomas are named in their first Scotland squad in almost a year for next month's World Cup round one play-offs against the Czech Republic.
fullText:
Sam Kerr and Martha Thomas have been named in their first Scotland squad in almost a year, as the experienced duo return for next month's Women's World Cup round one two-legged play-off against the Czech Republic.

Melissa Andreatta's side travel to Pardubice, east of Prague, on Friday, 9 October before welcoming the Czechs to St Mirren Park four days later, eyeing progression to another two-legged play-off against either Sweden or Lithuania with a place at next summer's tournament in Brazil at stake.

Liverpool midfielder Kerr - who has been playing out of position at right-back in the WSL - has yet to feature under Scotland women's Australian head coach, with the last of her 34 caps coming in February 2025 off the bench against the Netherlands, while Thomas - who joined WSL2 side Newcastle United in the summer - earned her 50th cap in October, in a friendly defeat by Switzerland.

Club-mate Freya Gregory - and Como defender Sophie Howard - who were forced to pull out of the last camp for the qualifying double-header against Israel, are also back in the squad.

Celtic midfielder, Maria McAneny - who last featured when scoring in a seven-goal thrashing of Luxembourg in March, returns too.

Defenders Leah Eddie and Kenzie Weir drop out, as do strikers Eilidh Adams and Laura Berry.

Mia McAulay was a late addition for the June double-header, but the Aston Villa youngster retains her place.

Andreatta's unbeaten side topped their qualifying group on goal difference - one better off than second-placed Belgium - and are now four games away from their first major tournament since the 2019 World Cup, having missed the past two European Championships and the 2023 World Cup.

title: Hawkins among five World Cup winners in England squad
description: Rob Hawkins is among five Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup winners who will attempt to help England defend the trophy in Australia this autumn.
fullText:
Rob Hawkins is among five Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup winners who will attempt to help England defend the trophy in Australia this autumn.

Hawkins, Wheelchair Super League's top try-scorer this season with 70, scored four tries as Halifax Panthers completed a domestic treble by beating Leeds Rhinos to win Sunday's Grand Final.

He is joined in England's 10-player final World Cup squad by club-mates Jack Brown - who scored six tries in that final - and Finlay O'Neill.

Both Hawkins and Brown were part of the England squad who defeated France dramatically at Manchester Central in November 2022 to win the World Cup.

So too was Lewis King, who will captain England down under, plus King's London Roosters club-mate Joe Coyd and Leeds Rhinos' Nathan Collins.

Collins will be joined in the England squad by Leeds team-mate Tristan Norfolk, Roosters' Mason Billington and the Sheffield Eagles pair of Luis Domingos and Chris Haynes.

England face Wales on Friday, 30 October (04:30 GMT) in their opening match at the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup - which will be staged alongside the men's and women's tournaments.

They then face the USA on Tuesday, 3 November (07:30 GMT) and Ireland on Friday, 6 November (06:00 GMT), aiming to secure a spot in the following Tuesday's semi-finals.

The wheelchair tournament will be staged at the Wollongong Entertainment Centre, with the final on Friday, 13 November (08:30 GMT).

England head coach Tom Coyd - who led the side to their World Cup success in Manchester four years ago - said: "Every player understands what it means to wear the England shirt and the responsibility that comes with it.

"Yesterday's brilliant Wheelchair Super League Grand Final was a testament to the special community that we are privileged to represent on the world stage."

England's wheelchair squad will fly out to Australia on 22 October.

description: Harry Kane has heaped praise on Lionel Messi when opening up on England’s loss to Argentina at the most recent World Cup. The Three Lions made it to the semi-finals of the competition but were beaten 2-1 thanks to late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez.
fullText:
Harry Kane has heaped praise on Lionel Messi when opening up on England's loss to Argentina at the most recent World Cup.

The Three Lions made it to the semi-finals of the competition but were beaten 2-1 thanks to late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez.

Messi and the rest of his team went on to lose against Spain in the final, while England ended up beating France in the third-place play-off.

Now, TyC Sports have shared quotes from Kane about his interaction with Messi after the semi-final clash.

When speaking about the Argentine, the English striker called him 'an incredible player' and said 'he seems like a very humble person'.

Kane stated: "Obviously, for me, that day [World Cup semi-final] was tough. A difficult moment getting eliminated in that way. But I have so much respect for Messi.

"I've watched him grow as a footballer. I think he's simply an incredible player and also an incredible person, from what people who know him tell me. I've only dealt with him a couple of times, but he seems like a very humble person to me.

"From that day, I remember hugging him and wishing him good luck for the final. It wasn't our World Cup in the end, but that's what a World Cup is about: the best players facing off on the biggest stage and, of course, there will always be a loser.

"That day, after losing, I tried to keep my head held high and show respect for the other team. I think that was something important, and especially toward Leo for how incredible he's been for so many years in football."

Kane likely did not know it at the time, but that meeting with England would turn out to be one of Messi's final international games.

The 39-year-old has announced his retirement from international football post-World Cup and is now due to have one final send-off game on October 6, playing a friendly against Benin.

title: Camilla Orlando previews Spain clash in Under-20 World Cup quarters
description: The Women’s U-20 National Team is ready for another challenge at the World Cup. This Friday (18), the team wrapped up its preparations for the clash against Spain in the quarterfinals of the tournam...
fullText:
The Women's U-20 National Team is ready for another challenge at the World Cup. This Friday (18), the team wrapped up its preparations for the clash against Spain in the quarterfinals of the tournament. On the eve of the match, head coach Camilla Orlando analyzed the opponents' characteristics and shared her expectations for the game.

"It will be a very challenging match. I would describe it as a chess game. Spain really likes to keep possession and control space, just like we do. It will be a very difficult match, like all the others, but it certainly has a different flavor because it's the quarterfinals," said the coach.

For Camilla, preparation for the clash involves maintaining the principles that have guided the team throughout the competition. The coach highlighted concentration and discipline as key factors in facing the Spanish side, without giving up Brazil's attacking style.

"We have to keep doing our work, with a lot of focus, discipline, and joy. Our players have been able to bring all of Brazil's joy, our way of playing with a lot of grit, so I don't think we need to do anything differently. We'll maintain consistency and attention to detail, but we want to keep showing our attacking game with the desire to score at every moment," Camilla added.

The match between Brazil and Spain will take place this Saturday (19) at 1:30 p.m. Brasília time, at Arena Sosnowiec in Poland. The winner of the match will advance to the semifinals of the FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup.

title: Netflix Signs Andrés Cantor For Women's World Cup 2027 Coverage
description: After 26 years at Telemundo, the Emmy Award-winning broadcaster makes the move to the streaming platform, bringing his signature "¡GOOOOL!" call with him.
fullText:
Andrés Cantor is leaving Telemundo and heading to Netflix, bringing his ​s​ignature "¡GOOOOL!" with him.

Netflix announced ​today that the Argentin​e​ American, Emmy Award-winning broadcaster will join its broadcast team for the FIFA Women's World Cup 2027, ​​h​andling Spanish-language coverage​. The streamer, which acquired exclusive U.S. rights to the 2027 and 2031 tournament​s in 2024, named Cantor as its first play-by-play voice for the tournament​. The signing comes fresh off his coverage of the record-breaking men's World Cup on Telemundo this summer.

Netflix's choice to lead with Cantor​ speaks to his standing as one of the most recognized voices in Spanish-language sports broadcasting. Naming him first, ahead of any English-side talent, signals how much weight Netflix is putting on Spanish-speaking audiences as it builds its inaugural roster for the tournament.

​Cantor will begin his new role with the Final Draw on December 11, streaming live on Netflix across the United States and Canada from Rio de Janeiro's Museum of Modern Art.

"For more than four decades, I've had the privilege of sharing my love for soccer with audiences around the world, and I'm incredibly excited to continue that journey with Netflix ahead of a historic summer for the sport," Cantor sa​ys. "I've been fortunate to call some of the game's most unforgettable moments and create memories that I will always value. Now, as Netflix continues to expand its presence at the forefront of live sports, I'm thrilled to bring the FIFA Women's World Cup to fans across the United States and Canada and to capture the passion, emotion, and magnitude that make this tournament so special."

Cantor's voice has been a steady soccer soundtrack in the U.S. since the late 1980s, first on Univision and later on Telemundo.

A Hall of Fame broadcaster, Cantor's résumé spans men's and women's FIFA World Cups, the Summer Olympics, Copa América, the UEFA Champions League, the English Premier League, and Major League Soccer, among many other competitions worldwide.

​H​e has called every men's FIFA World Cup since 1986​, along with four Women's World Cup tournaments, including the inaugural competition in 1991. ​He covered the last three Women's tournaments for Telemundo, anchoring the network's onsite, in-venue announce team for the 2023 edition in Australia and New Zealand.

Before his 26 years at Telemundo, Cantor spent 13 years as a sports anchor at Univision.

Now he heads into his fifth Women's World Cup, and his first outside the Telemundo umbrella in ​m​ore than two decades.

His departure comes after his contract with the network ended, closing a run that made him the defining voice of Telemundo's FIFA World Cup coverage since the network picked up the U.S. Spanish-language rights from Univision in 2011.

"Andres has been an integral part of the Telemundo family helping bring audiences closer to the sport and playing a meaningful role in its remarkable growth across the country," Telemundo said in a statement. "We are grateful for everything he has contributed to Telemundo, our audiences and the game he loves. We thank him for his extraordinary legacy and wish him continued success in the next chapter of his career."

The Cantor signing builds on a deal Netflix struck back in 2024, when it secured exclusive U.S. rights to the Women's World Cup for both 2027 and 2031, the first time the tournament will live on a streaming platform.

Th​e​ deal covered the U.S., including Puerto Rico and ​Canada. Netflix's FIFA Women's World Cup coverage will air in English and Spanish in the United States, and in English and French in Canada.

It also ended a run for two legacy broadcasters. Telemundo had carried Spanish-language coverage of the Women's World Cup in the U.S. since 2015, while Fox Sports held the English-language rights across the 2015, 2019 and 2023 tournaments. FIFA's decision to unbundle men's and women's media rights for the first time opened the door for Netflix to grab both.

Netflix ​has been pushing for more live sporting events on its platform. At the time of the acquisition, Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria pointed to the streamer's boxing crossover as an early signal of appetite for women's sports, citing the Amanda Serrano-Katie Taylor fight as proof of concept before the FIFA deal closed.

Cantor's arrival is just the first talent piece Netflix has confirmed. The rest of its broadcast team will be announced closer to the tournament, which runs June 24 through July 25, 2027, across eight host cities in Brazil.

title: Sorensen to join Republic of Ireland coaching staff

fullText:
Former Everton manager Brian Sorensen is set to join the Republic of Ireland squad for their Women's World Cup play-off qualifiers this year.

Sorensen is expected to take up the role of assistant coach in their set-up, alongside Liverpool's Amber Whiteley.

It is understood he will retain his position as technical director with Aston Villa women, but will link up with the Republic of Ireland during the international break.

He will work with manager Carla Ward, who faced Sorensen's Everton in the Women's Super League when she managed Villa.

The Republic of Ireland play Kazakhstan in the first round of play-off qualifying; the two-legged tie will take place on 9 and 13 October.

title: Canada captain loses sleep 'four to five nights a week' over England's World Cup win
description: Canada captain Sophie de Goede says she still loses sleep over their World Cup final loss to England last year.
fullText:
It is nearly a year since Canada lost the Women's Rugby World Cup final to England - but time has not been a healer for everyone.

"Four to five nights a week I can't fall asleep because I'm still thinking about the final," says Canada captain Sophie de Goede, who is preparing to take on the world champions this Saturday at Sandy Park in Exeter.

So, is this match revenge for the side ranked third in the world?

Canada head coach Kevin Rouet is keen to play this down: "Revenge is a good brand but they [England] won the final of the World Cup - that was the most important game to win, the next important games will be in the World Cup 2029."

After Canada, England play New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, before two more tests against Canada in Toronto and Ottawa. In recent history, England's women have never faced such tough successive opposition.

Red Roses head coach John Mitchell says the games are an "audition" for the 2029 World Cup.

"You look at the geography that we're going to cover, we're not always going to be in our training base. We're going to be going to different facilities. It's a challenge," he said.

"It's going to be really cool to see how they handle pressure as well. I think the Red Roses are very good around pressure because I think it reveals how much they care".

Saturday, 19 September at 15:00 BST

There continues to be misconceptions around the status of the Canadian women: they are professional athletes but contracts, as with most other nations, do not yet compare to England's women.

The Canadian programme involves a clever strategy of using England's domestic PWR league to develop its players.

There are 25 Canadians in PWR and the current Canada coaching staff includes Kevin Rouet and Alex Austerberry, who both coach Saracens Women, and Nathan Smith from Loughborough Lightning.

"It's not like we're coming in to spy," joked De Goede. "We just don't have the quality league [in Canada]."

Canada are not the only country to do this - PWR is littered with top internationals from across the globe.

Mitchell has told BBC Sport that he and Charlie Hayter, head of women's performance at England Rugby, have lobbied to increase PWR game time for English Qualified Players (EQP) from next season.

Mitchell has frequently pushed his theory that players who can reach 1,000 PWR playing minutes a season "gives them a higher probability" of playing for the Red Roses.

"I haven't enjoyed seeing young English players between 21 and 23 not getting enough minutes," he said.

"I think that number [1,000] is very meaningful."

The RFU confirmed to BBC Sport the current requirements around 13 EQP players on average across matchday squads will remain. However, the lure of signing foreign talent will be dampened by the removal of club injury credit, which helps cover the cost of replacing an injured player.

From the 2027-28 season, only players who sustain an injury while on international duty for one of England's representative teams will be eligible.

Besides this, if any EQP player is captured by another union, they will only be able to hold their EQP status until the end of that season.
